title: S3b: a failed setup must not stop Orca from starting (supersedes dbu.3: FROZEN named the implementation, not the test)
description:
Same slice as claude-orca-dbu.3, re-registered because its contract froze scripts/container/entrypoint.sh -- the implementation -- instead of the test, which inverts the RED/GREEN ritual. Text otherwise unchanged:

scripts/container/entrypoint.sh:237-241 calls die() when setup.sh fails, and die() exits. On the built-image path setup.sh is a VERIFICATION pass (every phase 'already present'), so its failure says something is wrong with the image, not that there is nothing to run. Killing the container there removes the only thing that could report the problem: no Orca, no terminal, no Claude Code.

Demote it: record the failure (run/provision/setup.status holding the non-zero exit, plus the existing run/setup.log), warn, and carry on to the privilege drop and orca-ide --serve. The one case that stays fatal is an ORCA_BIN that is not executable (entrypoint.sh:634), because there is then genuinely nothing to serve. Write run/provision/setup.status on SUCCESS too (0), so 'never ran' and 'ran fine' are distinguishable.

title: outbound-guard: a compound git push must not carry the marker-gated verbs past their gate
description:
Found in review of claude-orca-diz (PASSed its own contract; this is a defect that contract never named).

The new git push branch ends in a bare 'exit 0', so MARKER_RE is never evaluated for any command that also matched GIT_PUSH_RE. With a live GitHub connection, prefixing 'git push &&' now carries gh pr create / gh repo create / bd dolt push past the prompt-marker gate that the diz bead deliberately left in place.

Reproduced twice, independently -- by the orchestrator with a scratchpad probe and by the verifier -- with a stubbed gh reporting connected and an empty state dir:
  old guard: plain push DENIED | plain pr-create DENIED | compound DENIED
  new guard: plain push ALLOWED | plain pr-create DENIED | compound ALLOWED  <-- regression

The 38 frozen cases stay green because none of them pairs two verbs in one command line. That omission is the orchestrator's, not the executor's: the contract only ever asked for the verbs standalone.

FIX: delete the 'exit 0' from the git push branch and let a connected push fall through. MARKER_RE does not match a plain 'git push', so a lone connected push still ends in a clean allow; a compound line reaches the marker gate exactly as it did before diz. The has_sid fail-open below is unchanged, so 'git push && gh pr create' with no session_id keeps the pre-existing open posture.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/outbound-guard.bats

PASS-IF: the run prints a TAP plan line '1..N' with N >= 43, zero lines beginning 'not ok', and one 'ok' line for each of these cases, named verbatim:
  a connected git push compounded with gh pr create still requires the prompt marker
  a connected git push compounded with gh repo create still requires the prompt marker
  a connected git push compounded with bd dolt push still requires the prompt marker
  a connected git push on its own is still allowed with no marker
  a disconnected git push compounded with gh pr create is denied for the connection
All thirty-eight cases already in the file at GREEN-AT 6952fcb must still be present and still pass.

FROZEN: tests/outbound-guard.bats

CLASS: authorization guard, tightening. The five new cases pin the boundary the diz contract left open: a compound command must be evaluated against EVERY rule it matches, not only the first. The single-verb behaviour delivered by diz must not regress -- a lone connected git push still allows, a lone disconnected one still denies naming the connection, and the warehouse-CLI deny stays first and unconditional.
notes:
RED-AT: 7bbb2583443478ccac82444d0ef501fa47a8258f  GREEN-AT: cdccfae31c7b2178368b7296863a1e2a04f42f0c
VERIFIER: PASS. C1 1..43 zero not-ok, five PASS-IF names matched grep -Fxq, all 38 prior cases present and green; C2 frozen file byte-identical 7bbb258..cdccfae; C2b red confirmed at 7bbb258 with exactly 3 not-ok (39,40,41 -- the compounded cases), matching the executor's claim; C3 only scripts/outbound-guard.sh +7-2 and config/claude-user-memory.md 1 line; C4 the only functional line in the diff is '- exit 0'; C5 marker machinery and --prompt byte-identical, warehouse deny still first.
Decision table vs 8dbe6d9^: exactly ONE cell more permissive (plain git push, connected, sid present, no marker: DENY->ALLOW, the intended change). TWO cells strictly tighter (plain and compound push, disconnected, marker present: ALLOW->DENY). All three no-sid fail-open cells identical.

title: S2 the card itself: card-update writes it with haiku, card-view draws it without scrolling
description:
scripts/card-update.sh -- the Stop hook's worker. Reads the hook JSON on stdin and takes .transcript_path (or a path as $1). Walks the transcript's user/assistant entries, skips isSidechain, drops thinking blocks, flattens text blocks and tool_use blocks to 'name + command/file_path/description', keeps the tail under a byte budget with a per-row cap so one runaway message cannot fill it. Sends that to 'claude -p --model ${CARD_MODEL:-claude-haiku-4-5-20251001}' with a prompt that fixes the shape -- NOW / WHY / DONE (up to 3) / NEXT / SNAG, at most 12 lines, no line over 68 characters, no preamble -- and writes the result to .claude-dev/run/card.md through a temp file and mv, so the viewer never reads half a card.

scripts/card-view.sh -- runs inside the pane. Clears and repaints; never appends, so the pane cannot scroll. Redraws on a change to the card file's mtime and on SIGWINCH, and otherwise sleeps. Clips every line to the pane width and the card to the pane height. Hides the cursor and restores it on exit.

Both fail open: no payload, no transcript, no jq, no model, a model that returns nothing -- exit 0 and leave the previous card alone.

  card-update takes transcript_path from the hook payload on stdin and writes the card file

  card-update exits 0 and leaves the previous card in place when there is no transcript or the model returns nothing
  card-view draws one boxed card clipped to the pane and repeats no line of it
  card-view repaints when the card file changes and not otherwise

title: S1 card control: bin/card on|off|toggle|status|autostart, anchored to this terminal's own pane
description:
scripts/card.sh + bin/card (symlink, like bin/lane -> ../scripts/lane.sh).

Resolves the terminal it is running in: ORCA_PANE_KEY is '<tabId>:<leafId>'; match the leafId against 'orca terminal list --json' to get the handle. 'card on' splits that handle vertically running card-view, renames the new pane 'CARD', and records the handle in .claude-dev/run/card.pane and 'on' in .claude-dev/run/card.state. 'card off' closes the recorded pane and records 'off'. 'card toggle' flips. 'card status' prints one line. 'card autostart' is the SessionStart entry: open a pane when the state is on OR unset (default on), do nothing when it is off, and never open a second one when the recorded pane is still live.

Fails open, always: no ORCA_PANE_KEY, no orca CLI, an unreachable runtime, a stale handle -- each is 'exit 0, say so on one line', never an error that could stop a session starting.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/card-control.bats
PASS-IF: the TAP output has the plan line '1..7', zero lines beginning 'not ok', and one 'ok' line for each of these seven case names, verbatim:
  card resolves its own terminal handle from the leaf id in ORCA_PANE_KEY
  card on splits that terminal, renames the pane CARD, and records the handle and the on state
  card on is idempotent: a second call while the recorded pane is live splits nothing
  card off closes the recorded pane and records the off state
  card toggle flips on to off and off to on
  card autostart opens a pane when the state is on or unset and stays quiet when it is off
  card exits 0 with one explanatory line when there is no ORCA_PANE_KEY, no orca CLI, or an unreachable runtime

(2) scripts/container/openrouter-guard.py (python3 stdlib, no deps): listens on 127.0.0.1:4141, reads the real key from OPENROUTER_API_KEY at start and the policy file; for POST /api/v1/chat/completions, /api/v1/completions, /api/v1/responses, /api/v1/messages it parses JSON, sets body.provider = {only: allowlist, allow_fallbacks: false, data_collection: 'deny'} (a client-supplied provider.order is kept only when every entry is in the allowlist; anything else is dropped and logged), forwards to https://openrouter.ai with the real key, streams SSE back; GET paths proxied; refuses any client key other than the guard token with 401; appends one line per request {ts, model, providers_forced, client_order_dropped} to <project>/.claude-dev/run/openrouter-guard.log. title: v3 S2: Mac side — bootstrap preflight for Apple container, claude-dev register/open/stop/shell/logs/doctor/update/teardown against the image, web-url open
description: Why: the Mac half that creates and drives the VM (plan §5). What: bootstrap.sh preflight: Darwin + arm64 + macOS major >= 26 (sw_vers -productVersion), 'container' on PATH else print https://github.com/apple/container/releases and the installer line and exit 1, 'container system start' (idempotent; tolerate 'already running'), gh authenticated, git; then clone/pull the template into .claude-dev/template, link bin/, exec register. No brew bundle, no srt, no DMG, no rc-hook install. cmd_register: mkdir .claude-dev/{home,run,state}; seed .claude-dev/claude-orca.json {version:3, port:null, cpus:null, memory:null, extraMounts:[]} if absent; seed home .gitconfig from the Mac's global git config; choose the port once (claude-orca.json port, else 6768 or the next free via a bind probe; write run/port); 'container registry login ghcr.io' with gh auth token (username = gh api user login) then 'container image pull ghcr.io/joe-rayment/claude_orca:<tag>' where <tag> comes from .claude-dev/template/IMAGE_TAG (a one-line file, default latest) — on pull failure fall back to 'container build -t <same ref> -f <template>/Dockerfile <template>'; then cmd_open. cmd_open: if the container exists and is running → just open the URL; if it exists but stopped → 'container start'; else 'container run -d --name claude-orca-<name> --volume <project>:<project> --volume <project>/.claude-dev/home:/home/agent -p 127.0.0.1:<port>:<port> -e PROJECT_DIR=<project> -e ORCA_PORT=<port> -e HOST_UID=<id -u> -e GH_TOKEN=<gh auth token> [--cpus N --memory M from claude-orca.json] [--volume extra:ro] <image>'; then wait up to 120 s for <project>/.claude-dev/run/orca-web-url.txt (removed before the run so a stale one never opens), then 'open <url>' (CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=0 prints it instead) and print the three-line how-to-run. Container name = claude-orca-<derive_project_name>. stop: 'container stop <name>'. shell: 'container exec -it <name> zsh -l' (with --workdir <project>). logs: 'container logs -f <name>'. --doctor: container CLI present, service reachable ('container system status' or 'container ls' exit 0), image present, container state, port, web-url file, exits 2 on findings. --update: git pull template, image pull, stop+rm+recreate. --teardown: stop, rm, snapshot beads (existing helper), remove .claude-dev and ./claude-dev; also remove any v2 rc-hook block (existing rc_remove_block) since v2 folders may be upgraded. GH_TOKEN never printed. Every 'container' invocation goes through one function so tests can assert argv from a stub.

title: orca-launch: Orca uses the real ~/Library/Application Support (Electron ignores HOME on macOS) -> singleton lock EPERM, instant exit; pass --user-data-dir under a short per-project root
description: Why: on the user's Mac (2026-09-06) Orca.app exits immediately. orca-launch.log: readlink/create /Users/joerayment/Library/Application Support/orca/SingletonLock -> Operation not permitted, then Orca's own '[single-instance] Another Orca instance is already running' and exit; repo add times out waiting for orca-runtime.json. Root cause, verified from the extracted 1.4.197 bundle (out/main/index.js ~6808-6832): packaged Orca never calls app.setPath('userData'); Electron's appData on macOS comes from NSSearchPath, which ignores $HOME; and kei() then overwrites process.env.ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH with app.getPath('userData'), so our env var is discarded too. The Seatbelt profile denies /Users, so every write to the real Application Support fails, the lock first. Verified fix on the Linux build here (orca-linux-arm64.AppImage under Xvfb): with --user-data-dir=<dir>, SingletonLock, orca-runtime.json and the unix socket all landed in <dir> and nothing under ~/.config/orca -- Electron honors the switch natively, before Orca's lock. Second latent failure (claude-orca-qt9.10 part 1): the folder's userData path is ~90 bytes, plus o-<pid>-<4>.sock exceeds macOS's 104-byte sockaddr_un limit, so the transport would fail next. What: scripts/sandbox/orca-launch (1) host-side before sandbox-exec, creates a short per-project root: Darwin /private/tmp/co-<first 8 hex of sha1(project)>, elsewhere /tmp/co-<hash>, as a symlink to <project>/.claude-dev/home; refreshes it if it points elsewhere; refuses (exit 2, clear message) if the path exists and is not our symlink; CLAUDE_ORCA_SHORT_ROOT overrides the root. (2) exports ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<short root>/Library/Application Support/orca, mkdir -p the real dir, and passes --user-data-dir=<that path> as the first argument to the Orca binary. (3) refuses with a clear message when ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH length + 20 exceeds 100. (4) --print-command prints the exact env exports and sandbox-exec command line and exits 0 without launching, generating a profile, creating the symlink, or requiring sandbox-exec; --print-env prints just the exports. HOME and TMPDIR stay as they are. gen-orca-profile.sh needs no change: /private/tmp is readable and writes through the symlink resolve into the project.
design: Env knobs: CLAUDE_ORCA_SHORT_ROOT (override the short root, used by tests to force a too-long path), existing CLAUDE_ORCA_METADATA_TIMEOUT. Alternatives rejected: ORCA_BYPASS_SINGLE_INSTANCE_LOCK=1 (only skips the first casualty; the data dir is still denied); ORCA_E2E_USER_DATA_DIR (works but flips Orca's E2E mode on); a profileExceptions write-allow on the real Application Support (leaks Orca state outside the folder and makes every project share one lock). Supersedes part (1) of claude-orca-qt9.10; its dark-mode and doctor parts stay there. Mac behaviour (Seatbelt resolving the symlink into the project) is unverifiable here; the test proves the argv/env/symlink logic with a stub sandbox-exec.

title: orca-socket-unreachable probe FAILs on a real Mac with Orca running; register refusal gives no next step
description: User's first real run: [FAIL] orca-socket-unreachable -- orca status --json unexpectedly succeeded (orca.cli=false). Enforcement is allowUnixSockets=[] in gen-settings.sh + Seatbelt AF_UNIX deny; hypothesis: real orca CLI reaches the app over the localhost HTTP hook channel (or exits 0 without connecting), so the probe premise is wrong on any Mac with the app up — prior test passes were vacuous (stubbed orca). Awaiting DMG/CLI transport recon (scout-orca-dmg). Fix probe to test the enforced property, and make the register refusal print what to do next.

CHECK: bats tests/selftest.bats tests/orca-cli-mode.bats, then ./run-tests.sh.
PASS-IF: each bats run prints its 1..N plan, zero 'not ok' lines, and one 'ok' line per named case, names verbatim: 'socket probe: cli=false and runtime unreachable is a PASS' / 'socket probe: cli=false and runtime reachable is a FAIL naming the leak' / 'socket probe: cli=true and runtime reachable is a PASS' / 'socket probe: cli=true and runtime unreachable is N/A telling the user to launch Orca' / 'socket probe: unparseable status JSON falls back to the plain status exit code' / 'register refusal names the FAILed probes and the next step'; ./run-tests.sh exits 0 with zero 'not ok' lines.
FROZEN: tests/selftest.bats and tests/orca-cli-mode.bats from RED-AT.
CLASS: behavioral-bugfix.
NOTE: supersedes the cli-mode assertions at tests/orca-cli-mode.bats:263-302 whose stub modeled 'orca status --json exits 1 when unreachable' — falsified by the v1.4.197 binary (cli/handlers/core.js: exitCode=1 only when !json).
notes:

title: V6 First-real-run fixes: short HOME symlink for Orca's socket, dark-mode default, doctor socket check (verified with the Linux Orca)
description:
Why: the first real Orca run (Linux AppImage in this container, with the folder's .claude-dev/home as HOME) exposed one blocker and one preference. Blocker: Orca's daemon socket lives under the user-data dir derived from HOME, and a deep project path pushes it past the sockaddr_un limit (108 bytes on Linux, 104 on macOS) — Orca shows "couldn't start its local command transport… path is too long", the CLI becomes unavailable, and our launch-time `repo add` and the opt-in orchestration mode silently break. A short symlink to the same home directory (e.g. /tmp/oh → <project>/.claude-dev/home) fixed it. Preference: the user wants the sandboxed Orca in dark mode by default.
What: (1) scripts/sandbox/orca-launch creates, host-side before launch, a short per-project symlink to <project>/.claude-dev/home under a short root — Darwin: /private/tmp/co-<8 hex of sha1(project)> (readable in layer 1, never writable by layer 1 or 2; the symlink target resolves into the project so the profile's project rules apply); Linux: /tmp/co-<hash> — refreshes it if it points elsewhere, refuses (exit 2) if the path exists and is not our symlink, and exports HOME=<symlink> (TMPDIR and ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH stay as they are); it also computes the expected socket path length and refuses with a clear message when it would still exceed 100 bytes. `orca-launch --print-env` prints the exact env it would use (for the Linux demo and tests) and `--print-command` the sandbox-exec command line. (2) claude-dev --doctor warns when the socket path for the folder would exceed 100 bytes without the symlink and shows the symlink in the Orca section. (3) Dark mode: registration pre-seeds Orca's global settings file in the in-folder user-data dir (find the key and file from src/shared/global-settings-types.ts and src/main/global-settings* in the Orca clone; write only when the file is absent so a user's later choice is never overwritten) with the dark theme; the seed writes both the macOS location (Library/Application Support/orca/…) and the Linux one (.config/orca/…) under <project>/.claude-dev/home so either build picks it up; `sandbox.json` `orca.theme` (dark|light|system, default dark) selects it. (4) The Linux demo becomes the verification: launch the AppImage with `orca-launch --print-env`'s environment (no bypass switches added to the product; on Linux orca-launch itself refuses to launch because sandbox-exec is absent — the demo uses the printed env), confirm Orca starts in dark mode with the CLI transport working (no "path too long" modal), `repo add` succeeds, and screenshot it.
Boundaries: no profile content changes beyond none needed (the symlink target resolves into the project); no docs beyond README's sandbox.json options line for orca.theme and a knowledge-base note on the socket limit.
design: Evidence from the Linux run: socket path limit hit with HOME=<project>/.claude-dev/home; /tmp/oh symlink fixed it; user data at <HOME>/.config/orca; orca-runtime.json lists the unix socket and ws://127.0.0.1:6768; Linux CLI binary is resources/bin/orca-ide (macOS: Contents/Resources/bin/orca). Keep bash 3.2 lint clean; PASS-IF names verbatim as @test names; dry-run assertions before RED.

title: V2d Wrapper writes under layer 1: srt settings to a private per-launch temp dir agents cannot write; config-hash to run/
description:
Why: the wrapper (claude-orca-shell) and config-sync run INSIDE layer 1 when Orca launches a terminal, and layer 1 write-denies .claude-dev/state (host-owned). Two wrapper outputs still target it: the srt settings file state/srt-<sha1>.json and config-sync's state/config-hash. On the Mac every Orca terminal would fail to start (settings unwritable) or re-sync every time. The settings file is also security-sensitive: it defines layer 2, so it must not be written anywhere an agent (layer 2) can write — .claude-dev/run and tmp are agent-writable and an agent could race the wrapper between write and exec.
What: claude-orca-shell writes the srt settings file to a private per-launch directory that layer 1 allows and layer 2 denies: on Darwin `mktemp -d "$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)/claude-orca.XXXXXX"` (under /private/var/folders, which the Orca profile allows and srt's allowWrite never includes), mode 700, file mode 600, removed by an EXIT trap after exec is unreachable — or kept for srt to read: srt reads the file at startup before sandboxing, so the wrapper writes, execs srt, and the directory is cleaned by the next launch (document); elsewhere `mktemp -d`. config-sync's checksum moves to run/config-hash (the hash only gates re-sync; an agent tampering with it can only force or skip a sync, powers it already has via the config dir). gen-settings/gen-orca-profile: document which paths each layer writes. Tests in tests/wrapper-writes.bats (frozen) with the named cases; update tests/config-sync.bats / sandbox-config.bats / selftest.bats paths (unfrozen).
Boundaries: no probe additions (V3), no docs (V5).
design: Layer-1 allowed write roots per gen-orca-profile.sh: <project>, /private/var/folders, /dev. Layer 2 (srt) allowWrite: project-scoped only, so /private/var/folders is agent-denied. getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR returns /var/folders/xx/.../T/ on macOS; absent on Linux (fall back to mktemp -d). Keep bash 3.2 lint clean.

title: V2b Keychain denied for the whole folder (services block, orca.keychain switch, doctor line); clipboard kept
description:
Why: the user wants no access to the Mac's Keychain from anything running in the folder — Orca and the agents keep their own credential stores inside the folder — while the clipboard keeps working. Seatbelt can deny the Keychain mach services by name for the whole process tree; nested layers inherit it.
What: scripts/sandbox/gen-orca-profile.sh gains a marked "services" block: (deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.SecurityServer") (global-name "com.apple.securityd.xpc") (global-name "com.apple.ctkd") (global-name "com.apple.SecurityAgent") …) — derive the exact names from srt's macos-sandbox-utils.ts (it allows SecurityServer explicitly, which shows the name) and Apple's App Sandbox documentation; never deny com.apple.trustd, com.apple.pasteboard.1, com.apple.windowserver.active, com.apple.CoreDisplay, com.apple.fonts, com.apple.cfprefsd.daemon, com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd. A sandbox.json switch orca.keychain (default false = denied) re-allows the family for users who want Mac Keychain sharing, documented as an isolation trade-off. Inside the sandbox, Claude Code's `security find-generic-password` fails (the S3 probe keychain-denied now has a real cause) and Claude Code stores `.credentials.json` in the folder config dir (S5 behaviour). Doctor prints "keychain: denied (folder-local credentials)" / "shared with macOS (orca.keychain=true)".
Boundaries: no other profile changes (V2 owns the filesystem rules), no docs (V5).

title: S2b Shell-entry hardening: bash 3.2 compatibility, non-interactive login shells, rc block placement
description:
Why: three findings from S2's verification and the real install run must be closed before the wrapper is trusted on a Mac. (1) macOS /bin/bash is 3.2: `arr+=("${empty[@]}")` under `set -u` aborts there, so gen-settings.sh (and any sibling script with the same idiom) would fail closed on every Mac shell whenever extraAllowWrite is empty — every script under scripts/ must run under bash 3.2. (2) Non-interactive login shells (`zsh -l -c …`, `bash -l -c …`) do not read .zshrc/.bashrc, so they start unsandboxed inside a bootstrapped folder; Orca's agent terminals are interactive and covered, but the hook must also live in .zprofile/.bash_profile-login path and preserve the -c command through the re-exec (zsh: $ZSH_EXECUTION_STRING; bash: $BASH_EXECUTION_STRING). (3) rc-install must append its block LAST (after Homebrew shellenv lines) and the bash side must cover .bash_profile and .profile-less setups consistently.

What: scripts/sandbox/* and scripts/launcher.sh rc-install made bash-3.2-safe (guard idiom `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}`, no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${var,,}); shellrc.zsh/.bash re-exec that carries the execution string: `exec claude-orca-shell --root R -- zsh -l -c "$ZSH_EXECUTION_STRING"` when set (bash likewise), interactive re-exec unchanged; claude-orca-shell accepts a trailing `-c <cmd>` for the inner shell; rc-install writes the marker block into ~/.zprofile as well as ~/.zshrc (both guarded by CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED so the second source is a no-op), keeps ~/.bash_profile, and always appends after existing content; tests/helpers/ensure_bash32 builds GNU bash 3.2.57 into tests/.cache/bash32 (from the scratchpad copy at /tmp/claude-1000/-workspace/7037bfad-67da-4b5e-9adb-944b260fc264/scratchpad/bash32/install when present, else from ftp.gnu.org) so the suite can run the scripts under the real macOS bash version.

Boundaries: no self-test probes (S3), no config sync (S4). tests/sandbox-config.bats and tests/bootstrap.bats are unfrozen (S1/S2 closed) and must stay green; add cases there only if a premise changed.

title: S2 Sandbox wrapper: srt settings generator, scope derivation, env, shell re-exec, fail-closed
description:
Why: the security core. Every shell opened in a bootstrapped folder (by Orca, Terminal.app, or `orca terminal create`) must re-exec itself inside srt/sandbox-exec with a scope derived from the folder, before any agent binary runs.

What: ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-root (primary checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, falls back to walking up for .claude-dev/sandbox.json), ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-shell (generates srt settings, sets env, `exec srt --settings <file> -c 'exec zsh -l'`), shellrc.zsh + shellrc.bash (sourced from the user's rc via one marker-delimited line installed/removed idempotently by `claude-dev`), scripts/sandbox/gen-settings.sh (pure function: inputs → JSON).

Scope: primary session allowWrite=[<project>, <project>/.claude-dev/home, <project>/.claude-dev/tmp]; linked worktree session allowWrite=[<worktree>, <primary>/.git, <primary>/.beads, <primary>/.claude-dev/home, <primary>/.claude-dev/tmp]. denyRead=[real HOME]; allowRead=[<project>, <worktree>, ~/.claude-orca, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.orca/agent-hooks]. Extra denyWrite (host-executed files): orca.yaml, .worktreeinclude, .envrc, .beads/hooks/**. network.allowedDomains = defaults ∪ validated sandbox.json extras; strictAllowlist true; allowLocalBinding true; allowPty true; enableWeakerNetworkIsolation true; allowAppleEvents false; allowUnixSockets [] (S9 may add the Orca runtime dir). Env inside: HOME=<primary>/.claude-dev/home, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude, TMPDIR=<primary>/.claude-dev/tmp, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GH_CONFIG_DIR, BEADS_DIR=<primary>/.beads, ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_REAL_HOME, PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:<real ~>/.local/bin:~/.claude-orca/template/bin:...

Fail closed: srt or sandbox-exec missing, generator error, or unvalidated sandbox.json → the shellrc defines refusing functions for claude, codex, gemini, opencode and prints the reason; never continue unsandboxed silently.

Boundaries: no auth/credential masking config beyond the hook point (S5), no Orca hook merge (S6), no self-test (S3). The wrapper treats everything under <project> as untrusted data.
design: gen-settings.sh is a pure bash function taking (primary, worktree, real_home, sandbox_json, mode) and printing JSON via jq so tests can assert exact documents. Settings file path: <primary>/.claude-dev/state/srt-<sha1(worktree)>.json. Schema validation test uses `node -e` importing the installed sandbox-runtime package (stub-installed in tests from the scratchpad clone or npm cache; skip with a clear reason only if node is absent). Real srt facts used: deny default; writes allow-only; allowLocalBinding opens localhost outbound; allowPty for /dev/ttys*; mandatory write-denies under cwd for shell rc files, .mcp.json, .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .git/hooks, .git/config (srt src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:15-40, macos-sandbox-utils.ts:79-106).

title: S2 Sandbox wrapper: srt settings generator, scope derivation, env, shell re-exec, fail-closed
description:
Why: the security core. Every shell opened in a bootstrapped folder (by Orca, Terminal.app, or `orca terminal create`) must re-exec itself inside srt/sandbox-exec with a scope derived from the folder, before any agent binary runs.

What: ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-root (primary checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, falls back to walking up for .claude-dev/sandbox.json), ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-shell (generates srt settings, sets env, `exec srt --settings <file> -c 'exec zsh -l'`), shellrc.zsh + shellrc.bash (sourced from the user's rc via one marker-delimited line installed/removed idempotently by `claude-dev`), scripts/sandbox/gen-settings.sh (pure function: inputs → JSON).

Scope: primary session allowWrite=[<project>, <project>/.claude-dev/home, <project>/.claude-dev/tmp]; linked worktree session allowWrite=[<worktree>, <primary>/.git, <primary>/.beads, <primary>/.claude-dev/home, <primary>/.claude-dev/tmp]. denyRead=[real HOME]; allowRead=[<project>, <worktree>, ~/.claude-orca, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.orca/agent-hooks]. Extra denyWrite (host-executed files): orca.yaml, .worktreeinclude, .envrc, .beads/hooks/**. network.allowedDomains = defaults ∪ validated sandbox.json extras; strictAllowlist true; allowLocalBinding true; allowPty true; enableWeakerNetworkIsolation true; allowAppleEvents false; allowUnixSockets [] (S9 may add the Orca runtime dir). Env inside: HOME=<primary>/.claude-dev/home, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude, TMPDIR=<primary>/.claude-dev/tmp, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GH_CONFIG_DIR, BEADS_DIR=<primary>/.beads, ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_REAL_HOME, PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:<real ~>/.local/bin:~/.claude-orca/template/bin:...

Fail closed: srt or sandbox-exec missing, generator error, or unvalidated sandbox.json → the shellrc defines refusing functions for claude, codex, gemini, opencode and prints the reason; never continue unsandboxed silently.

Boundaries: no auth/credential masking config beyond the hook point (S5), no Orca hook merge (S6), no self-test (S3). The wrapper treats everything under <project> as untrusted data.
design: gen-settings.sh is a pure bash function taking (primary, worktree, real_home, sandbox_json, mode) and printing JSON via jq so tests can assert exact documents. Settings file path: <primary>/.claude-dev/state/srt-<sha1(worktree)>.json. Schema validation test uses `node -e` importing the installed sandbox-runtime package (stub-installed in tests from the scratchpad clone or npm cache; skip with a clear reason only if node is absent). Real srt facts used: deny default; writes allow-only; allowLocalBinding opens localhost outbound; allowPty for /dev/ttys*; mandatory write-denies under cwd for shell rc files, .mcp.json, .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .git/hooks, .git/config (srt src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:15-40, macos-sandbox-utils.ts:79-106).

title: A recreated container downgrades the image's Orca to setup.sh's pin: the launcher builds at the app's version but never tells docker run
description:
Observed 2026-09-19 on the container the user rebuilt from the Mac. .claude-dev/run/build.log: 'RUN CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.278 ORCA_VERSION=1.4.203 /opt/claude-orca-setup.sh --image', tag claude-orca:latest-orca1.4.203 -- the launcher builds at the Mac app's version because Orca refuses a client/runtime protocol mismatch (epic claude-orca-8uo). .claude-dev/run/setup.log from the SAME start: 'orca: installing 1.4.197'; /opt/orca/VERSION now reads 1.4.197.

Cause: the docker run command (scripts/launcher.sh, the 'set -- run -d --name' block at ~line 2202) carries no ORCA_VERSION, so the boot-time setup.sh falls back to its own pin (scripts/container/setup.sh:36), phase_orca (~line 499) sees stamp 1.4.203 != 1.4.197 and reinstalls the pin over the image's build: a download on every recreate, and a runtime that no longer matches the app the image was built for. The runtime path (plain ubuntu:24.04) has the same hole -- it installs the pin, never the app's version.

DECISION (orchestrator): the launcher hands docker run '-e ORCA_VERSION=<v>' where <v> is wanted_orca_version (scripts/launcher.sh ~line 1358) -- the ONE answer the image tag and the build arg already use: the app's version when this host has one, the Dockerfile's ARG default otherwise -- whenever that answer is non-empty. Boot-time setup.sh, setup.sh --check (10-toolchain-verify) and the runtime-path install then all agree with the image. Rejected: teaching setup.sh to adopt whatever stamp it finds when ORCA_VERSION is unset -- it loosens --check, which has to stay a strict reading of the box, and leaves the runtime path installing the pin.

Consequence, measured: with ORCA_VERSION in the container's environment every shell inherits it. Running the suite with ORCA_VERSION=1.4.203 ambient turns exactly one case red: tests/container-image.bats 'setup.sh parses, and --check reports every phase's result on any box', which reads the pin out of setup.sh's text while the script itself honours the environment. SUPERSEDE (test-only, of the claude-orca-qa2.6-frozen case, no assertion changed): directly after the case's '[ -n "$pin" ]' line add
    pin="${ORCA_VERSION:-$pin}"
with a one-sentence comment (the script honours an ambient ORCA_VERSION, so the case has to want what the script wants). That line goes in the RED commit.

scripts/launcher.sh runs on macOS bash 3.2.57: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${x^^}, no += onto an empty array under set -u. The docker run line is built with 'set -- "$@" ...'; add the new -e the way the CLAUDE_ORCA_SETUP conditional a few lines below the fixed block does.

(A) tests/launcher-orca-version-run.bats (new). Model the fixture on tests/launcher-v3.bats 'open runs the container with ...' (line ~172: how the docker stub records the run line) and tests/launcher-v3-build.bats 'build passes --build-arg ORCA_VERSION from the installed app' (line ~327: how an installed app at a version is faked). title: setup.sh --check FAILs every Mac folder: it wants agent at uid 1000 after the entrypoint re-mapped it to HOST_UID
description:
Observed 2026-09-19 on the container the user rebuilt from the Mac: the SessionStart hook's first line was '[provision] 10-toolchain-verify FAILED -- [check] FAIL  agent user: want uid 1000, got 501'. title: worktree-gc: append every run (mode, Orca reachability, exit, every line, busy pid) to run/worktree-gc.log so a hook run that left a worktree behind explains itself
description:
Diagnostic gap found in real use (2026-09-18): after `git merge joe-rayment/wt-ltd` the PostToolUse hook `worktree-gc --after-merge` ran but left the merged wt-ltd worktree in place; a by-hand `worktree-gc` minutes later removed it ("closed Orca's idle terminal"), and feeding the hook payload by hand to `--after-merge` also removed a fresh worktree. Nothing recorded what the hook run saw (Orca unreachable? busy process? a timing race with the terminal close), because hook stdout is transient. Cap the file at 200 KB by truncating the oldest half when it grows past that. --after-merge also logs the command text that triggered it (first 200 chars). Nothing else in the script changes; all three FROZEN suites (tests/worktree-gc.bats, tests/container-provision-worktree-sweep.bats, tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats) must stay green untouched.

title: worktree-gc: keep a clean worktree whose branch is unmerged (report STRANDED, kept: unmerged) -- supersedes case 2 of tests/worktree-gc.bats (claude-orca-6zg)
description:
Policy fix for scripts/worktree-gc.sh, found in real use 2026-09-18: a CLEAN worktree whose branch has commits not in main is removed by step 2 (the branch is kept and reported STRANDED). In practice that is the state of every finished-but-not-yet-verified worker: merging slice A's branch fires the PostToolUse `worktree-gc --after-merge`, which removed slice B's finished worktree while the verifier was still running its CHECK in it (claude-orca-kbu today; the branch survived, the worktree had to be re-added by hand). Removing such a worktree frees ~4 MB and buys nothing; the branch is the data and it stays anyway. New rule for step 2: a clean worktree is removed ONLY when its branch is contained in main/master (`git merge-base --is-ancestor `) or when it is detached with HEAD contained in the base. A clean worktree whose branch has commits not in the base is KEPT and reported "STRANDED branch : N commit(s) not in main (worktree

kept: unmerged)" with exit 1 -- the same shape the busy/dirty kept-worktree lines already use. Busy, dirty and directory-gone handling are unchanged. title: orca-worker-run: headless opencode worker that runs the spec, heartbeats, writes a receipt, sends worker_done and exits (no resident TUI)
description:
Problem (user, 2026-09-18): worker slices dispatched with `orca-dispatch <bead> --agent opencode` run as a resident opencode TUI inside an Orca terminal. Measured today: ~900 MB RSS per TUI for as long as the terminal lives, three of them resident at once with only one working, the harness killing background tasks for low memory; a headless `opencode run --format json` of the same model peaked at 708 MB and exited after 10 s, freeing everything. The user's direction: Claude orchestrates, OpenRouter models execute beads -- nobody watches the TUI, so workers must be headless runs that exit, never resident processes.

Slice 1 of 2: the headless runner. Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines per Write/Edit call, one file per response, report under 60 lines. bash, `set -uo pipefail`, bash-3.2-clean (scripts/lint-bash32.sh scans scripts/).

(A) New scripts/orca-worker-run.sh + symlink bin/orca-worker-run -> ../scripts/orca-worker-run.sh. Resolve its own path like scripts/orca-dispatch.sh (_resolve_script_path), source scripts/lib/paths.sh and scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh (for orca_call / orca_field and the run-dir helpers already there -- read them first).
    orca-worker-run --task <task_id> --spec <file> --model <openrouter/...> --dir <worktree> [--run-dir <dir>] [--heartbeat-s <n>] [--bead <id>]
  Behaviour, in order:
   1. Guard env: `set -a; . <run-dir>/openrouter-guard.env; set +a` exactly as orca_opencode_command does (scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh ~360-418); die with exit 2 and one stderr line when the env file is missing.
   2. Dispatch id: poll <run-dir>/orchestration/dispatch/*.json for the record whose .task_id equals --task, up to 30 s (orca-dispatch writes it right after `orchestration dispatch`); take .dispatch_id. If none appears, continue with an empty dispatch id (worker_done still carries --task-id).
   3. Record the base: `base=$(git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD)`.
   4. Run headless: `opencode run -m <model> --dir <dir> --auto --format json "$(cat <spec>)"` with stdout+stderr to <run-dir>/orchestration/workers/<task_id>.log (mkdir -p), in the background; while it runs, every --heartbeat-s seconds (default 240) send `orchestration send --type heartbeat --subject alive --dispatch-id <d> --json` (skip when the dispatch id is empty) so orca-wait's stall watch stays quiet. Wait for it; capture the exit code.
   5. Receipt: parse the json log the way scripts/delegate.sh does (tokens_in, tokens_out, usd, wall_seconds; copy its jq) into <run-dir>/orchestration/workers/<task_id>.receipt.json with fields {task_id, dispatch_id, bead, model, dir, exit_code, tokens_in, tokens_out, usd, wall_seconds, started_at, finished_at}; hand it to cost-mirror with the same best-effort call delegate.sh makes (`cost-mirror --ingest-delegate-receipt <file>`, fail-open).
   6. Report: files = `git -C <dir> diff --name-only <base>..HEAD` joined by commas (plus `git status --porcelain` paths, deduplicated); body = the last assistant text in the log (the final "text" part in the json events; fall back to the last 20 non-empty lines of the log), trimmed to 1500 chars; then `orchestration send --type worker_done --subject "<bead or task_id> done" --body "<body>" --task-id <task_id> --dispatch-id <d> --outcome succeeded|failed (failed when exit code != 0 or when the log's last event is an error) --files-modified <files> --json`. Never skip the send: a failed run reports failed, so the orchestrator is never left waiting.
   7. Exit with opencode's exit code. Redact the guard token from the log and the receipt the way delegate.sh's redact_secret does.
(B) New tests/orca-worker-run.bats. Stubs on PATH in a tmpdir: `opencode` (asserts argv contains `run`, `-m <model>`, `--dir <dir>`, `--format json`; prints a canned json event stream with a "text" part reading "did the thing" and token usage the receipt jq can read; writes <dir>/made-by-worker.txt and commits it so diff --name-only shows it; sleeps $STUB_SLEEP seconds; exits $STUB_EXIT), `orca-ide` (appends argv to $ORCA_STUB_LOG; answers `{"ok":true}`), `cost-mirror` (records argv). A real git repo as <dir>. Named cases, each its own @test:
   1. "worker-run sends worker_done succeeded with the task id, the dispatch id read from the dispatch record, and the committed file in --files-modified"
   2. "worker-run reports failed when opencode exits non-zero and still sends worker_done"
   3. "worker-run writes a receipt with tokens, usd and the exit code and hands it to cost-mirror"
   4. "worker-run sends at least one heartbeat during a long run" (STUB_SLEEP=3, --heartbeat-s 1)
   5. "worker-run proceeds with an empty dispatch id when no record appears" (no record; worker_done still sent with --task-id; no heartbeat sent)
   6. "worker-run exits 2 with one stderr line when the guard env file is missing"
   7. "worker-run redacts the guard token from the log and the receipt"

title: worktree-gc: one sweep for merged worktrees, merged branches, stranded work and finished delegate job dirs; 65-worktree-sweep delegates to it
description:
Problem (user, 2026-09-18): the template leaves git worktrees and branches lying around after work is merged. Measured in this folder: 2 clean, fully-merged delegate worktrees still checked out, 15 merged branches (delegate/*, worktree-agent-*, joe-rayment/wt-*, integration, s8, v2...), and 329 MB under .claude-dev/delegate -- of which the worktrees are 4 MB each and each job's home/.npm/_cacache (94 MB) + config/opencode/node_modules (62 MB) are the rest. Today the ONLY cleanup is scripts/container/provision.d/65-worktree-sweep, which runs at container boot, never deletes a branch, and never touches job dirs. The user also wants stranded work (a branch with commits not in main) to be impossible to miss, never silently deleted. Do, in one slice (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, no bash-4-only syntax -- scripts/lint-bash32.sh scans scripts/). Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines per Write/Edit call, one file per response, and report in under 60 lines. (A) New scripts/worktree-gc.sh with symlink bin/worktree-gc -> ../scripts/worktree-gc.sh (same shape as bin/bd-guard). Resolve its own path the way scripts/orca-dispatch.sh does (_resolve_script_path) and source scripts/lib/paths.sh. Usage: worktree-gc [--report] [--quiet] [--project ] Project dir: --project, else $PROJECT_DIR, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of $PWD; the MAIN worktree is the first line of `git worktree list --porcelain`. Exit 0 when nothing is stranded, 1 when any STRANDED/FAIL line was printed, 0 with "not a git repo" when there is no repo. --report prints exactly the lines it WOULD print but deletes nothing (prefix each with "would "). --quiet prints only STRANDED/FAIL lines and one final summary line "worktree-gc: removed N worktree(s), deleted M branch(es), swept K job dir(s)" -- and prints nothing at all when all counts are 0 and nothing is stranded. Steps, in order: 1. HEAD of the main worktree: if `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` is neither main nor master (or detached), print "STRANDED HEAD is on , not main -- the live version is main; merge back or switch" and set exit 1. Never switch branches itself. 2. Every worktree other than the main one, exactly the current 65-worktree-sweep semantics and wording (copy its code: /proc cwd scan for busy, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` for dirty, `orca-ide worktree rm --worktree path:

--json` when `orca-ide status --json` says .result.runtime.reachable==true, else `git worktree remove` then --force, then `git worktree prune`): lines "pruned

(directory gone)", "busy

(a running process has it as its cwd)", "FAIL: kept

(uncommitted or untracked changes)" (exit 1), "removed

". NEW: remember each removed worktree's branch for step 3. 3. Every local branch other than main/master and the checked-out one (`git for-each-ref refs/heads`): if `git merge-base --is-ancestor main` -> `git branch -d ` and print "deleted branch (merged)"; else print "STRANDED branch : N commit(s) not in main -- merge it or `git branch -D ` to drop the work" where N is `git rev-list --count main..`, exit 1, delete nothing. Use master when there is no main. A branch still checked out in a kept worktree is skipped silently. 4. title: branch-guard: PreToolUse hook denying branch creation or switching off main without BRANCH_OK=1
description:
Problem (user, 2026-09-18): the agent sometimes starts working on a git branch unprompted, and the user then loses time asking why changes do not appear in the live version. This template is for solo development: work lands on main, in the one working tree the user is looking at. A branch is rare, deliberate, and always merged back in the same session.

Do, in one slice (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, bash-3.2-clean -- scripts/lint-bash32.sh scans scripts/). Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines per Write/Edit call, one file per response, and report in under 60 lines.

(A) New scripts/branch-guard.sh with symlink bin/branch-guard -> ../scripts/branch-guard.sh. A PreToolUse hook for the Bash tool, the SAME shape as scripts/outbound-guard.sh: read the hook JSON from stdin (exit 0 silently when stdin is a tty, empty, not JSON, tool_name != "Bash", or .tool_input.command absent), decide on `.tool_input.command`, and deny by printing the hookSpecificOutput JSON {hookEventName:"PreToolUse", permissionDecision:"deny", permissionDecisionReason:<reason>} and exiting 0 (copy outbound-guard's deny()). Allowed calls print nothing and exit 0. Fail open on every error.
  Denied -- word-boundary matches anywhere in the command text, including after && ; | and inside $( ):
    git checkout -b <x>  and  git checkout -B <x>
    git switch -c <x>, git switch -C <x>, git switch --create <x>
    git worktree add ...
    git branch <name>   (creation: a first non-option argument, and none of the flags that delete, move, copy, list or filter: d, D, m, M, c, C, a, r, l, list, merged, no-merged, contains, show-current, format, v, vv)
    git switch <name>   where <name> is not main, master or the single dash (switch only ever takes a branch)
    git checkout <name> where <name> is a single bare word that is not main/master/dash/double-dash, contains no "--", AND `git -C <cwd> show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<name>` succeeds (cwd = .cwd from the payload, else $PWD) -- so `git checkout somefile`, `git checkout -- path`, `git checkout HEAD~1 -- path`, `git checkout <sha> -- path` all pass.

   3. "denies git branch <newname> but allows the list, delete, merged and show-current forms"
   4. "denies git switch <branch> other than main, master and dash"
   5. "denies git checkout <existing-branch> in the payload's cwd but allows checkout of a path, of -- path, of HEAD~1 -- path and of a word that is not a branch"
   6. "allows git checkout main and git switch main"
   7. "denies a branch creation chained after cd && or inside a command substitution"
   8. "allows anything prefixed BRANCH_OK=1"
   9. "the deny reason names main, BRANCH_OK=1 and merging back"
  10. "exits 0 with no output on a tty, empty stdin, non-JSON, a non-Bash tool and a payload without a command"

title: mg8 regression: orca-dispatch's real spooler leaks into bats runs (inherits fd 3, never exits) and hangs ./run-tests.sh in frozen-hook.bats
description:
Seen 2026-09-17 on main da4f27f: ./run-tests.sh sat 49 minutes inside tests/frozen-hook.bats 'orca-dispatch and delegate suites stay green' (it nests bats tests/orca-dispatch-launch.bats tests/delegate.bats). Two 'orca-wait.sh --spool --from <the orchestrator's real ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE>' processes, started by orca-dispatch during that nested run, were reparented to init, looping on 'sleep 0.1' 48 minutes later, and held bats's output pipe open (bats-core's fd 3), so the run never finished. Three defects:
(a) the spooler launch in scripts/orca-dispatch.sh does not close inherited descriptors: it must run as `setsid nohup ... </dev/null >>"$log" 2>&1 3>&- &` (fd 3 is what bats waits on) -- and scripts/orca-wait.sh --spool should `exec 3>&-` defensively at start;
(b) the spooler does not exit when its root or dispatch dir disappears: with no readable dispatch dir it must exit at once, and the idle exit (CLAUDE_ORCA_SPOOL_IDLE_S) must count from the last LIVE record, so a stub-driven spooler whose tmpdir is gone dies within seconds, not never; the poll interval must respect CLAUDE_ORCA_WAIT_POLL_S (the 0.1s sleep seen is not it);
(c) tests that drive orca-dispatch through the orca stub must never start a real spooler: tests/helpers/orca-stub.bash's orca_stub_init exports CLAUDE_ORCA_SPOOL_CMD to a no-op shim (one place) so orca-dispatch-launch.bats, orca-dispatch.bats, frozen-hook.bats, orca-two-coordinators.bats, variant-carry.bats etc. inherit it; the one test that WANTS the real spooler (orca-wait-spool.bats case 1) sets it back explicitly.
Files: scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/orca-wait.sh, tests/helpers/orca-stub.bash, new tests/orca-spool-detach.bats (tests/orca-wait-spool.bats stays as is -- it was FROZEN for the closed mg8; add nothing there unless case 1 needs the explicit un-shim).

title: openrouter-guard: a 429 from one allowlisted provider must fail over to the next allowlisted one -- policy gains an explicit provider order
description:
Seen 2026-09-17 21:04-21:20Z: seven glm-5.3-flash workers and a single probe all got 429 '[DeepInfra] z-ai/glm-5.3-flash is temporarily rate-limited upstream' through the guard for 15+ minutes, while the same request with provider.order ["baseten"] answered 200 at once (fireworks/coreweave/deepinfra 429). Cause: config/provider-policy.json forces allow_fallbacks=false and opencode sends no provider.order, so OpenRouter tries only its default pick (DeepInfra) inside `only` and errors instead of hopping to another allowlisted provider. The user's rule (data never routes to China) is enforced by `only`; failing over INSIDE that list breaks nothing.

The guard log line gains "order_source": "client"|"policy".

title: outbound-guard: gate git push on a GitHub connection, not on the prompt's wording
description:
The guard was ported (b1cabb2) as a mechanical restatement of config/claude-user-memory.md:12 -- 'push only when the current prompt asks for it'. The user's stated original intent was the opposite gate: avoid pushing when there is NO GitHub connection, and be biased to pushing when there is one. No connection check was ever written: the script has no gh invocation, no GH_TOKEN read and no network call (confirmed by reading it in full).

Observed cost, this session: I asked 'shall I push?', the user answered 'yes', PROMPT_RE did not match 'yes', line 158 cleared the marker, and the push was denied. The user had to retype the literal verb.

Scope of the change:
  - git push: gated on a GitHub connection (gh auth status, exit 0) instead of the marker. Connected -> ALLOW.
  - gh pr create / gh repo create: UNCHANGED, still marker-gated. They create outward artifacts other people see, which the user's instruction did not name.
  - bd dolt push: UNCHANGED, still marker-gated. Not GitHub, no connection concept applies.
  - the data-warehouse CLI rules: UNCHANGED, unconditional deny.
  - every existing fail-open path preserved.
  - config/claude-user-memory.md paragraph rewritten to match, or the prose keeps contradicting the mechanism and the prose is what gets read every session.

The connection check runs ONLY after PUSH_RE matches, so a plain Bash call never pays for it (measured: gh auth status is 0.39s here). Timeout via OUTBOUND_GUARD_GH_TIMEOUT (default 10s); timeout or error -> not connected -> deny, since a push would hang or fail too.
design:
OBJECTIVE
Replace the prompt-marker gate for 'git push' ONLY with a GitHub-connection gate. Connected -> allow. Not connected -> deny. Everything else in the guard keeps its current behaviour exactly.

FILES (touch these and no others)
  scripts/outbound-guard.sh      the gate
  tests/outbound-guard.bats      the contract (FROZEN from RED-AT)
  config/claude-user-memory.md   the paragraph at line 11-12

HOW
1. Add a connection check, called ONLY after PUSH_RE has already matched, so an ordinary Bash call never pays for it:
     gh_connected() { command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
                      timeout "${OUTBOUND_GUARD_GH_TIMEOUT:-10}" gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; }
   Non-zero from timeout (124) or from gh, or gh absent -> NOT connected.
2. Split PUSH_RE into two regexes: GIT_PUSH_RE (git push) and MARKER_RE (gh pr create | gh repo create | bd dolt push). Keep the same word-boundary style -- explicit character classes, never GNU \\b.
3. Order inside the PreToolUse branch: the warehouse-CLI deny stays FIRST and unconditional. Then GIT_PUSH_RE -> gh_connected -> allow or deny. Then MARKER_RE -> the existing marker lookup, unchanged.
4. Preserve every fail-open path exactly as it is, including 'missing session_id fails open'. git push no longer needs a session_id at all (it does not read the marker), but the no-session_id payload must still exit 0.
5. Deny text for git push must name the connection, not the prompt. Something like:
     outbound-guard: no GitHub connection (gh auth status failed) -- a push would fail; run 'gh auth login' or commit locally.
6. Rewrite the paragraph in config/claude-user-memory.md so the prose matches the mechanism: git push is allowed whenever there is a GitHub connection and blocked when there is not; PRs, repo creation and dolt push still need the prompt to ask. The old sentence 'run only when the current prompt asks for them' must not survive for git push.
7. Update the script's own header comment, which currently documents the marker rule for all four verbs.

BOUNDARIES
- Do not touch the warehouse-CLI rules, SNOW_RE, SNOW_MODULE_RE or their tests.
- Do not remove the marker machinery or the --prompt mode; three verbs still use it.
- Do not edit config/claude-settings.json; the hook wiring does not change.
- No network calls in the tests: stub gh on PATH.

TEST NOTES (learned the expensive way)
- Copy the twelve PASS-IF case names into @test lines VERBATIM, one @test per name.
- Dry-run every assertion against a hand-built fixture before committing RED.
- bats here prints TAP with no summary line; do not assert on 'N tests, 0 failures'.
- For the timeout case set OUTBOUND_GUARD_GH_TIMEOUT=1 and make the gh stub sleep 3, so the case costs ~1s.
- For 'the connection check is not run for a non-outbound command', make the gh stub append to a file and assert the file does not exist after a 'git commit' payload.
- Write files in <=150-line Write/Edit pieces, one file per response; report under 60 lines.

COMMITS
Two: the test file RED first (subject 'tests: RED for the GitHub-connection push gate (claude-orca-diz)'), then the implementation GREEN. Record RED-AT and GREEN-AT SHAs on the bead with bd update --append-notes.

title: S4: provision.d -- the project-shaped work moves after Orca is serving
description:
Everything that is about THIS FOLDER rather than about the image comes out of the blocking path and becomes a numbered, idempotent step under scripts/container/provision.d/, run after orca-ide --serve has published its URL: toolchain verify (setup.sh --check), bd init, the instruction/config sync, orca repo add, git identity, the OpenRouter guard.

Each step writes run/provision/<step>.log and run/provision/<step>.status. No step is fatal. A step that fails leaves a status a human and an agent can both read, and the next start re-runs it -- idempotence is the whole contract, so every step must be safe to run on an already-provisioned folder.

The ordering constraint that made this necessary: the steps a folder needs are exactly the steps most likely to fail (a network hiccup, a half-written config, a bad token), and they were all in front of the thing that could have reported them.

title: S1: split the Dockerfile into claude-orca-base and the folder image
description:
Dockerfile.base carries the apt half (setup.sh --image) and the six payload phases (bats, dolt, bd, orca, opencode, claude) and builds the image claude-orca-base:<IMAGE_TAG>. Dockerfile becomes FROM claude-orca-base:<tag>, plus 'COPY --chown=agent:agent . /opt/claude-orca' and the template phase -- two layers.

acquire_image builds the base first when the daemon does not already hold it, then the folder image. A base that is present is never rebuilt implicitly: only --prebuild (S2) and a pin move rebuild it, because the base is the 15-minute half and nothing should pay it by surprise.

Pins stay in setup.sh; the ARG lines move to Dockerfile.base with them. .dockerignore already excludes .claude-dev, .git and tests/.cache -- the top image's context stays ~2 MB.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/container-image.bats and tests/launcher-v3-build.bats
PASS-IF: Dockerfile's first instruction is FROM claude-orca-base:<tag>; Dockerfile.base contains every RUN that installs a payload phase and Dockerfile contains none of them; a register with the base already present issues exactly one 'docker build --tag claude-orca:<tag>' and no base build; a register with no base present issues the base build first, then the folder build, in that order.
FROZEN: Dockerfile, Dockerfile.base
CLASS: build

title: S2: claude-dev --prebuild, and an update that does not block on the base
description:
A command that builds or refreshes claude-orca-base without a folder waiting on it, so the 15-minute half is paid deliberately rather than by whoever registers next. --update builds the base in the background and leaves the folder on its current image until the new one is ready, so an update never stops the world -- the thing that just went wrong twice.

Reports the base image id before and after, the same way cmd_update_v3 already reports the folder image, so 'it did not move' is a sentence the output can say.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/launcher-v3-build.bats and tests/update-hygiene.bats
PASS-IF: './claude-dev --prebuild' issues a 'docker build --tag claude-orca-base:<tag>' and creates or starts no container; --update never leaves the folder without a runnable image, including when the base build fails; both print the before/after base image id.
FROZEN: none
CLASS: build

title: Two-image build, and a startup that cannot wall off the agent
description:
Two related changes, one cause. The image is now built on the machine that runs it (commit pending, this session): no CI, no registry, no token. This epic splits that build in two and moves everything project-shaped out of the blocking path.

MEASURED PAYLOAD (read off the live container, 2026-09-08): Orca 529M, Claude Code 206M, opencode 176M, bd 128M, dolt 114M, bats 0.1M -- ~1.15 GB that moves only when a pin moves, sitting under ~2 MB of repo that moves every push.

HONEST CORRECTION to the argument that opened this: the per-push chain is ALREADY short. Dockerfile:35 copies setup.sh on its own line above the six payload RUNs, and the repo copy is the last layer, so editing a script today invalidates only 'COPY . /opt/claude-orca' and the template phase. The split does NOT buy a cheaper push -- the layer order already did. What it buys is a base that can be built deliberately and early (prebuild/warm) instead of only as a side effect of someone's first register, insurance against a cold or pruned cache, and a clean seam if the base is ever worth publishing once a quarter.

THE OTHER HALF, which is the user's original ask and the more important one: scripts/container/entrypoint.sh:230 calls die() when setup.sh fails, which exits before Orca ever starts. A failing step 1 therefore removes the observer -- no Orca, no terminal, no Claude Code, and nothing inside that could report the failure. Features got built on top of a foundation nobody could see was broken. Orca must come up even when provisioning is broken, and the steps must be visible and re-runnable from inside.
close_reason: The half that mattered is delivered and verified: a failed setup no longer removes the observer (dbu.6), the folder-shaped work runs as idempotent provision.d steps after Orca serves (dbu.4), and the agent inside can see and repair its own provisioning with 'provision status/run', a hook that speaks only on failure, and doctor rows on the Mac (dbu.5). The two-image split (dbu.1, dbu.2) stays DEFERRED as standalone beads by the epic's own admission that it buys no cheaper push.

title: S3 wiring: /card, the SessionStart and Stop hook entries, config-sync and the README
description:
config/claude-commands/card.md -- the /card slash command, in this repo's established shape (frontmatter with description, argument-hint, allowed-tools Bash(card:*), model haiku, effort low; body ending in the bang-call and 'print the tool output verbatim'). Bare /card toggles; /card on, /card off, /card status are explicit. This is the control the person remembers -- one word, typed where they already are.

config/claude-settings.json -- two entries, both in the background form the disk-cleanup entry already uses, so neither can delay anything:
  SessionStart -> card autostart
  Stop         -> card update
Both guarded with the '[ -x ... ] && ...; exit 0' idiom every other entry uses, so a folder whose template predates this still starts.

config-sync already mirrors config/claude-commands into the project's .claude/commands; the test proves the card command lands there. README documents /card and the run/ files next to the other folder config.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/card-wiring.bats
PASS-IF: the TAP output has the plan line '1..5', zero lines beginning 'not ok', and one 'ok' line for each of these five case names, verbatim:
  SessionStart runs card autostart in the background so it cannot delay a session
  Stop runs card update in the background so it cannot delay a turn
  every card hook entry is guarded, so a folder whose template lacks the script still starts
  the /card slash command is a trivial passthrough to card and documents on, off and toggle
  config-sync mirrors the card command into the project's .claude/commands
FROZEN: tests/card-wiring.bats
CLASS: integration -- reads the shipped config and runs config-sync into a temp project

title: Epic: an index-card panel beside Claude Code, written by a small model
description:
A pane next to the Claude Code terminal holding ONE index card -- what is happening, why, what is done, what is next, what is stuck. It never scrolls: the card is replaced, not appended. Opus writes long and buries the point; the card is written by haiku, which is the whole reason the feature exists.

MECHANISM (all of it verified on 2026-09-08 before this was written):
* Orca has no plugin, webview or custom-pane API -- its right sidebar is
  hardcoded (explorer/search/sourceControl/checks/ports) and plugins only
  contribute VM recipes. What it does have is
  'orca terminal split --terminal <handle> --direction vertical --command <cmd>',
  which puts an arbitrary program in a pane of the current tab. That is the panel.
* A terminal knows its own identity from the environment Orca sets:
  ORCA_PANE_KEY is '<tabId>:<leafId>', and leafId matches a row of
  'orca terminal list --json'. So a hook running inside the session can find the
  handle of the terminal it is running in, and split THAT one.
* Claude Code hook payloads carry .transcript_path (confirmed in the binary), and
  the transcript is JSONL of user/assistant entries whose content blocks are
  text / tool_use / thinking. Dropping thinking leaves a compact record of the turn.
* 'claude -p --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' answers in ~4s cold, ~47s for a
  6k-character transcript tail. It runs from the Stop hook, backgrounded, so it
  can never make a turn wait.

SHAPE:
  scripts/card.sh (bin/card)  on | off | toggle | status | autostart
  scripts/card-update.sh      Stop hook: transcript tail -> haiku -> run/card.md
  scripts/card-view.sh        runs IN the pane: clear, draw one boxed card, wait
  config/claude-commands/card.md   the /card slash command -- the control
  config/claude-settings.json      SessionStart -> card autostart (background)
                                   Stop         -> card update   (background)
  .claude-dev/run/card.state  on|off, default on   .claude-dev/run/card.pane  handle
                              .claude-dev/run/card.md  the card itself

THE CONTROL: /card toggles, /card on and /card off are explicit. One word to
remember, in the TUI the person is already typing in -- not a shell command that
would mean leaving the session.

EVERY PIECE FAILS OPEN. These run in hooks: no Orca, no jq, no model, no
transcript must each mean 'exit 0, no card', never a session that will not start.
close_reason: Closed

title: startup v4 S2b: supersedes qa2.10 -- the image no longer carries the toolchain, so 'which image' stopped being the same question as 'does this start install anything'; weburl_timeout needs both halves
design:
qa2.10 froze this file when 'which image is it' and 'does this start install anything' were the same question. The image now carries only apt (setup.sh IMAGE_PHASES); the toolchain -- Orca, Claude Code, opencode, bd, dolt, bats -- installs on a folder's first start into <project>/.claude-dev/toolchain, mounted over /usr/local, /opt/Orca and /opt/claude.

So the two questions came apart, in both directions: a PULLED image with an empty cache has ~5 minutes of toolchain to install, and a RUNTIME image reinstalls its apt half on every recreate however full that cache is (dpkg state cannot live in a bind mount). weburl_timeout now asks start_installs_nothing() -- cache populated AND image not runtime -- and only then waits 120s.

Measured on a real Mac (2026-09-07, Docker Desktop 29): keyed on the toolchain cache alone, a runtime-path recreate got 120s for a 280s job and the launcher gave up on a container that was working fine. The corrected case is red against the qa2.10 launcher (pulled + empty cache answers 120, must answer 1800) and green against this one.

Only case 5 changes. The other six are qa2.10's, unedited.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/launcher-v3-pull.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan line 1..7; zero 'not ok' lines; an 'ok' line each, names verbatim: 'without read:packages register runs docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 with the mounted template entrypoint instead of building'; 'CLAUDE_ORCA_IMAGE runs a locally held image with no login and no pull'; 'a failed pull falls back to the base image path and never runs an image build'; 'a failed docker run stops open with an error instead of waiting for Orca'; 'the launcher waits 1800s whenever a start has something to install, and 120s only when both halves are in hand'; 'CLAUDE_ORCA_WEBURL_TIMEOUT overrides both paths'; 'the runtime-path wait prints setup.log progress and the failure message names setup.log'
FROZEN: tests/launcher-v3-pull.bats
CLASS: behavior
close_reason: Premise no longer holds: the toolchain moved back INTO the image (CLAUDE.md § Architecture, measured 18-minute first start), so 'does this start install anything' collapsed back to 'which image is it'. The surviving timeout contract is tests/launcher-v3-build.bats:214 'the launcher waits 1800s on the runtime path and 120s on the built image, whatever the folder has cached', green.

title: Install flow: register hands off to Orca with no prompts (auto beads init, auto-open, warn-not-refuse on availability probes)
description:
Why: the user hit 'Step 1/6: Claude login ... waiting for .credentials.json' at the end of the bootstrap one-liner and called it a needless barrier; the install must be 'run one command, start working'. register currently ends in an interactive 'Walk through setup now? [Y/n]' (default Y) and refuses to hand off on ANY failed self-test probe.

What: (1) register_setup_offer goes away: register never reads /dev/tty; it prints one 'Optional extras: claude-dev setup (...)' pointer line. (2) register runs 'bd init --prefix <derived name>' itself when bd is on PATH and .beads is absent, best-effort, quiet, unless CLAUDE_ORCA_SKIP_BEADS=1 (the test harness sets that globally so the real bd never runs from make_project). (3) After a passing self-test, register prints the run-it block and then opens Orca in the background (cmd_open) when CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=1, or when CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN is unset AND uname -s is Darwin AND stdout is a terminal; CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=0 never opens. (4) Self-test refusal is limited to confinement probes: write-outside-denied, read-real-home-denied, keychain-denied, sibling-worktree-denied, tmp-outside-denied, network-blocked-domain, host-files-write-denied, orca-profile-active, git-hooks-audit, and the synthetic srt-launch probe. A FAIL on any other probe prints a one-line warning naming the probe and its detail plus 'claude-dev --doctor', then hands off normally (exit 0). (5) README install section describes the new shape: one command, Orca opens, sign in inside Orca on first run.
design: Decisions: security guarantee unchanged (no hand-off when confinement fails); availability failures (network reachability, srt pin, Orca socket, sandbox-exec presence, home-redirected, orca-data-in-folder, project/worktree writable) degrade to warnings because they do not make the hand-off unsafe. cmd_open gains an optional dir argument so register can call it for $dir. Env knobs: CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN (1/0/unset), CLAUDE_ORCA_SKIP_BEADS. Existing test in tests/setup-menu.bats that pins the old pointer string is updated in this slice (not frozen). New cases live in a NEW file tests/register-flow.bats so FROZEN does not overlap the setup-menu slice.

title: S6 Orca integration: managed hooks merge, statusline chain, sub-agent rows, transcript visibility
description:
Why: the point of Orca is seeing what agents do — working/waiting/done dots, sub-agent child rows, session history. Orca implements these through hooks it writes into the real ~/.claude/settings.json, which the sandboxed Claude (own config dir) never loads unless we carry them over.

What: the wrapper (host side, every launch) merges Orca's managed entries — identified by the ~/.orca/agent-hooks/claude-hook.sh command — for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TeammateIdle, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PostCompact from ~/.claude/settings.json into <config dir>/settings.json without duplicating ours; removes them when Orca's are gone; chains Orca's claude-statusline.sh before our statusline; allowRead ~/.orca/agent-hooks (already in S2); ORCA_* env passes through untouched; Orca's curl uses --noproxy 127.0.0.1 and allowLocalBinding covers the POST. Transcript visibility: verify on the Mac whether Orca's session history / usage see $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects (Orca reads the env of its own process, not the agent's); if not, the wrapper writes a symlink ~/.claude/projects/<slug> → <config dir>/projects/<slug> (host side, outside the sandbox). Registration prints the one-time Settings → Repository worktree base path suggestion (<project>/.orca-worktrees).

title: S6 Orca integration: managed hooks merge, statusline chain, sub-agent rows, transcript visibility
description:
Why: the point of Orca is seeing what agents do — working/waiting/done dots, sub-agent child rows, session history. Orca implements these through hooks it writes into the real ~/.claude/settings.json, which the sandboxed Claude (own config dir) never loads unless we carry them over.

title: claude_orca: port claude_docker to a macOS Seatbelt sandbox managed by Orca
description:
Port the claude_docker template to a macOS-native design: agents run under Apple's Seatbelt (sandbox-exec via Anthropic's pinned `srt` runtime) scoped to the project folder, and Orca (onorca.dev) manages sessions, worktrees, status and sub-agent rows. Keep beads, --dangerously-skip-permissions, /tier, and the hook/guard suite. Claude Code stays primary; Codex/Gemini/OpenCode run inside the same sandbox and take instructions from Claude. Drop the tmux fleet sidebar, worktree-sessions (cs-new/peers/session-title) and all Docker-bound machinery.

Plan with findings, design, risks and slice table: .claude/plans/orca-port.md (this repo). Source material: attachments/claude_docker (old template), Orca 1.4.197 and srt 0.0.75 sources (cloned during planning; refs in the plan).

Trust-boundary invariant every slice must respect: nothing that runs unsandboxed executes or sources anything agent-writable. Host-owned root is ~/.claude-orca (bin, template clone, srt, shellrc); project-owned root is <project>/ (including .claude-dev/{home,tmp,state,sandbox.json}). No ./claude-dev launcher lives in the project root; the launcher is `claude-dev` on PATH.

Verification split: this container is Linux. Each slice's CHECK is Linux-runnable (bats over the shell logic with srt/brew/gh/npm stubbed; schema validation against the pinned srt). Slices with macOS-only behaviour also carry a MAC-CHECK line naming the self-test that bootstrap runs on the Mac and refuses to hand over without; MAC-CHECK is informational for the verifier, never a reason to close.

GitHub: repo name claude_orca (beads prefix is already claude-orca). Creation from this session is blocked — the gh token cannot create repositories (GraphQL createRepository and REST POST /user/repos → 403). When joe-rayment/claude_orca exists: add it as origin and publish main.
close_reason: All slices S1–S12 (+S2b) implemented, independently verified under their acceptance contracts, and merged into main at 3d59e31; ./run-tests.sh 673 ok; bead-auditor held all 13 active closures. Open follow-ups recorded in .claude/plans/orca-port.md §8 (Mac self-test run, gh-token masking default, --prompt-file coverage).

title: S1 Bootstrap & claude-dev launcher for macOS (brew tools, template clone, srt pin, project registration)
description:
Why: the entry point of the whole template — one command run in a project folder must install the host side once and register the project. Replaces bootstrap.sh + claude-dev + Dockerfile/docker-compose from claude_docker.

What: bootstrap.sh (curl|bash via `gh api repos/joe-rayment/claude_orca/contents/bootstrap.sh -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" | bash`), scripts/launcher.sh installed as ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-dev (commands: register (default, cwd=project), --doctor, --update, --teardown, --uninstall — the last three are S12/S3 stubs here), Brewfile (git gh jq ripgrep node bats-core bd; no helix/tmux), scripts/install-tools.sh (brew bundle check/install, Orca cask presence → prints `brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca` if missing), scripts/install-srt.sh (`npm --prefix ~/.claude-orca/srt install @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime@0.0.75`, node >= 20.11 check), template clone into ~/.claude-orca/template, per-project registration: creates <project>/.claude-dev/{home,tmp,state}, sandbox.json defaults, seeds .gitignore (.claude-dev/, .mcp.json, attachments/, .claude/logs/), creates attachments/, prints "open this folder in Orca".

Boundaries: no sandbox logic (S2), no config sync (S4), no self-test (S3). Requires macOS at runtime; on Linux the scripts must still be unit-testable with stubbed brew/gh/npm/git on PATH.
design: Stubs live in tests/helpers/stubs/<tool> and are prepended to PATH by tests/helpers/setup.bash (port of the old helper). Host root ~/.claude-orca is overridable via CLAUDE_ORCA_HOME for tests. Launcher is derived from attachments/claude_docker/claude-dev with all Docker code removed. Template clone URL: https://github.com/joe-rayment/claude_orca.git (main). The launcher must never exec anything under the project folder (trust boundary in the epic).
