title: /tier presets: one name for a top/worker/recon combination, a bare /tier that offers them like /model, the current binding shipped as 'hybrid'
description:
User request 2026-09-19: "For the /tier behaviour, I'd like to add presets for combination. I'd like the behaviour to be basically like /model behaviour. I'd like our current settings to be one of the presets." Current settings = /tier fable glm-flash luna@high.

DESIGN (orchestrator; do not redesign):
A preset is ONE NAME for an existing /tier argument form, so every parsing, validation, pin and effort rule in scripts/tier-set.sh is reused unchanged. /model's behaviour is: bare -> a picker of the choices with the current one marked; '<name>' -> switch directly and say so. /tier gets the same two halves.

1. config/tier-presets.json (new; data, read with jq, never sourced), found the way ROUTES_FILE is (tier-set.sh ~line 98-104): PRESETS_FILE="${TIER_PRESETS_FILE:-<root>/config/tier-presets.json}". Shape and shipped content, in this order:
   {"presets":[
    {"name":"hybrid","summary":"Fable orchestrates, GLM 5.3 flash works, GPT-5.6 Luna (high) scouts -- low-cost OpenRouter workers","args":["fable","glm-flash","luna@high"]},
    {"name":"hybrid-glm","summary":"as hybrid, with full-size GLM 5.3 workers for slices flash flounders on","args":["fable","glm","luna@high"]},
    {"name":"opus-hybrid","summary":"Opus orchestrates over the same low-cost OpenRouter workers","args":["opus","glm-flash","luna@high"]},
    {"name":"all-claude","summary":"no OpenRouter: Fable, with the Claude worker and recon it derives","args":["fable"]}
   ]}
   At most 4 presets are ever offered in the picker (the AskUserQuestion tool takes 2-4 options); the listing shows all.
2. scripts/tier-set.sh:
   a. '/tier <name>' -- exactly one argument that is a preset name and NOT a reserved word (show help overdrive auth models checker worker recon, the Claude aliases fable opus sonnet haiku in any case, any route name in ROUTES_FILE; reserved words always win): re-run this same script with the preset's args (so the unchanged path does the binding), and only if that exits 0 stamp the name into the state file with jq ('.preset = $n', tmp file + mv like the other writers), then print one line 'preset <name> -- <summary>' followed by the child's own output. write_state/write_state_v3 build the state with 'jq -n', so ANY later non-preset bind drops .preset by construction -- do not add code for that, test it.
   b. bare '/tier' and '/tier show': after the existing state lines and BEFORE show_guide, a section
        presets -- /tier <name>:
          * hybrid        fable glm-flash luna@high   <summary>   (current)
            hybrid-glm    fable glm luna@high         <summary>
      '*' and '(current)' mark the preset named in the state's .preset; none is marked when .preset is absent. A missing or invalid presets file prints nothing here and never fails the command.
   c. bare '/tier' ONLY (not 'show'), and only when stdout is NOT a terminal ([ -t 1 ] is false -- that is how the slash command and bats both run it): end the output with
        [tier-picker]
        current: <name or none>
        option: <name> -- <summary>
        ... (the current preset first when there is one, then file order, at most 4)
        [/tier-picker]
   d. show_guide gains ONE line for the preset form, e.g. '  /tier hybrid                          a preset -- one name for a whole combination; bare /tier lists them'. Keep every existing guide line byte-identical.
3. config/claude-commands/tier.md: description mentions presets and that a bare /tier offers them; argument-hint gains 'hybrid' first; allowed-tools becomes 'Bash(tier-set:*), AskUserQuestion'; model/effort unchanged; the body keeps the '!`tier-set "$ARGUMENTS"`' line first and then says, in this order: (i) if the output ends with a [tier-picker] block, call AskUserQuestion ONCE -- question 'Which tier preset?', header 'Tier', one option per 'option:' line in that order (label = the name, plus ' (current)' on the current one; description = the summary) -- then run 'tier-set <chosen name>' (for the free-text 'Other' answer: 'tier-set <the text as typed>') and print THAT output verbatim and nothing else; if the question is dismissed, print the output above without the [tier-picker] block; (ii) otherwise the existing verbatim-passthrough sentence, unchanged.
4. tests/tier-presets.bats (new). Model the fixture on tests/tier-phrases.bats (TIER_STATE_FILE / TIER_ROUTES_FILE style env overrides, a throwaway state file; unset ambient PROJECT_DIR, CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT, BEADS_DIR; never touch /workspace/claude-orca/.claude-dev/run/tier.json). Cases:
   1 '/tier hybrid binds exactly what /tier fable glm-flash luna@high binds': the two state files are equal once .updated and .preset are deleted; .preset == "hybrid"; output's first line starts 'preset hybrid'.
   2 'any other bind drops the preset': after hybrid, 'tier-set opus' leaves no .preset key.
   3 'a one-word preset binds the derived ladder': all-claude -> top fable, worker sonnet, recon haiku, pinned false, .preset all-claude.
   4 'bare /tier lists every preset, marks the current one, and ends with the picker block': after hybrid; '(current)' on the hybrid line only; the block has 'current: hybrid', hybrid as the first option, <= 4 option lines, and is the END of the output. With no .preset: 'current: none' and no '(current)'.
   5 '/tier show lists the presets but prints no picker block'.
   6 'reserved words win': with a TIER_PRESETS_FILE that names a preset 'opus' (args ["haiku"]), 'tier-set opus' still binds top=opus and stamps no .preset.
   7 'the shipped presets file is sound': 1-4 presets; names match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, unique, none reserved, none a route name in config/delegate-routes.json; every args is an array of 1-3 non-empty strings; every summary non-empty.
   8 'a missing presets file changes nothing': TIER_PRESETS_FILE=/nonexistent -> bare output has no presets section, no picker block, exit 0; 'tier-set hybrid' behaves exactly as an unknown single word does today (capture that behaviour BEFORE you change the script and assert it).
   9 'the command file wires the picker': config/claude-commands/tier.md's allowed-tools holds both 'Bash(tier-set:*)' and 'AskUserQuestion'; its first body line is the tier-set line; the body names '[tier-picker]' and 'AskUserQuestion'; 'model: haiku' is still there.
Boundaries: tests/tier-hooks.bats, tests/tier-phrases.bats, tests/tier-gate-orca.bats are FROZEN by earlier beads -- do not edit them; if one of their cases goes red, STOP and send an orchestration question naming the case and the assertion. tier.json gains only the optional 'preset' key; no reader changes. scripts/tier-set.sh runs in the container (bash 5 is fine) but keep its style. title: orca-wait redesign (redo of claude-orca-n3e): detached spooler + cheap reader + --until; the orchestrator never runs the poll loop in its own turns
description:
Observed over one live session (2026-09-17, ~8h, 9 dispatches): the orchestrator called orca-wait ~20 times. Each call is a blocking Bash tool call: in the foreground it is capped at 10 minutes by the harness and burns a turn per timeout (workers take 20-60 min); in the background it was killed twice by the harness's low-memory guard and once ended early by the stall watch's fallback (fixed in claude-orca-20o). The mailbox, receipts, bead notes, release/close and stall watch are all sound; the flaw is WHO runs the loop -- the orchestrator, in its own context, as a poll.

Design: split orca-wait into a detached spooler and a cheap reader.
1. `orca-wait --spool` (started once per Run by orca-dispatch if not running; pid file under run/orchestration/) runs the existing loop forever, detached with nohup/setsid, and appends every receipt line (worker_done, question, escalation, stalled, timeout-free) to run/orchestration/inbox.jsonl, doing the release/close/bead-note/stall work itself. It exits when no record in dispatch/ is live for N minutes.
2. `orca-wait` (no flag) returns immediately: prints and consumes unread inbox lines (cursor in run/orchestration/inbox.cursor). `orca-wait --until <n>` blocks up to n seconds only until the inbox grows, via a cheap inotify/poll on the file, not on Orca.
3. The orchestrator waits with the harness's own primitive: the Monitor tool (an until-loop on `test -s inbox.jsonl` past the cursor) or a background `orca-wait --until 3600`, so a worker message wakes the orchestrator through a task notification with no turn spent polling and nothing 1 GB-sized to be memory-killed.
4. Questions still print reply_with: orca-reply <msg_id> -- unchanged.
Contract when picked up: bats with a stub orca -- spooler appends a worker_done receipt and marks the record done while no reader runs; reader prints unread lines once and nothing the second time; --until returns within 1s of a new line and after n seconds otherwise; spooler exits when all records are done; orca-wait.bats/-records/-retained stay green.

REDO of claude-orca-n3e: its RED commit 17cd75e froze tests/orca-wait-spool.bats with a broken fixture in case 4 (orca-dispatch was driven with a stub orca that answered only orchestration-worker-start, so it died at task-create). The assertions stand; only the stub answers for orchestration-task-create / orchestration-run-create are missing. The redo commits a corrected test as a NEW RED-AT under this bead, then GREEN. Same design, files, CHECK, PASS-IF, FROZEN (tests/orca-wait-spool.bats from the new RED-AT), CLASS as below.

  CONTRACT (2026-09-17, orchestrator):                                        
  Files: scripts/orca-wait.sh (loop at ~379-427, receipts ~236-260 and ~363-  
  374, side effects ~318-360), scripts/orca-dispatch.sh (start the spooler    
  right after the dispatch record is written, ~line 349; pattern: nohup ...   
  </dev/null &, pid file run/orchestration/spool.pid, like scripts/openrouter-
  auth.sh:143-162), tests/orca-wait-spool.bats (new).                         
  CHECK: bats tests/orca-wait-spool.bats tests/orca-wait.bats tests/orca-wait-
  records.bats tests/orca-wait-retained.bats tests/orca-dispatch.bats         
  </dev/null                                                                  
  PASS-IF: zero 'not ok'; tests/orca-wait-spool.bats named cases: (1) orca-   
  wait --spool with the stub orca returning one worker_done appends one       
  receipt line to run/orchestration/inbox.jsonl and marks the dispatch record 
  done while no reader runs, then exits once no record is live                
  (CLAUDE_ORCA_SPOOL_IDLE_S set small); (2) orca-wait prints the unread line  
  once and nothing the second time (run/orchestration/inbox.cursor advanced); 
  (3) orca-wait --until 5 returns within ~1s when a background writer appends 
  a line, and --until 2 returns after ~2s with a distinct exit code when      
  nothing arrives; (4) orca-dispatch starts exactly one spooler per Run (a    
  live pid in spool.pid means no second start) -- make the spooler command    
  overridable (CLAUDE_ORCA_SPOOL_CMD) so the test can shim it. The classic    
  blocking behaviour stays reachable (e.g. orca-wait --poll-loop, or the      
  spooler code path with a bounded timeout) so the existing orca-wait cases   
  run unchanged or with a one-flag adaptation.

title: orca-wait redesign: the orchestrator should not run the mailbox poll loop in its own turns
description:
Observed over one live session (2026-09-17, ~8h, 9 dispatches): the orchestrator called orca-wait ~20 times. Each call is a blocking Bash tool call: in the foreground it is capped at 10 minutes by the harness and burns a turn per timeout (workers take 20-60 min); in the background it was killed twice by the harness's low-memory guard and once ended early by the stall watch's fallback (fixed in claude-orca-20o). The mailbox, receipts, bead notes, release/close and stall watch are all sound; the flaw is WHO runs the loop -- the orchestrator, in its own context, as a poll.

Design: split orca-wait into a detached spooler and a cheap reader.
1. `orca-wait --spool` (started once per Run by orca-dispatch if not running; pid file under run/orchestration/) runs the existing loop forever, detached with nohup/setsid, and appends every receipt line (worker_done, question, escalation, stalled, timeout-free) to run/orchestration/inbox.jsonl, doing the release/close/bead-note/stall work itself. It exits when no record in dispatch/ is live for N minutes.
2. `orca-wait` (no flag) returns immediately: prints and consumes unread inbox lines (cursor in run/orchestration/inbox.cursor). `orca-wait --until <n>` blocks up to n seconds only until the inbox grows, via a cheap inotify/poll on the file, not on Orca.
3. The orchestrator waits with the harness's own primitive: the Monitor tool (an until-loop on `test -s inbox.jsonl` past the cursor) or a background `orca-wait --until 3600`, so a worker message wakes the orchestrator through a task notification with no turn spent polling and nothing 1 GB-sized to be memory-killed.
4. Questions still print reply_with: orca-reply <msg_id> -- unchanged.
Contract when picked up: bats with a stub orca -- spooler appends a worker_done receipt and marks the record done while no reader runs; reader prints unread lines once and nothing the second time; --until returns within 1s of a new line and after n seconds otherwise; spooler exits when all records are done; orca-wait.bats/-records/-retained stay green.

Seen 2026-09-17: after worker_done from the recon dispatch, orca-wait printed 'released ctx_2c2eecfc6de4 (retained)' -- Orca's worker-release returned state=retained, the opencode process stayed resident at ~0.9 GB for 40 minutes, and with two more opencode workers the container hit its memory limit and the harness killed background jobs. The same happened for every opencode worker since (ctx_58a55669d1e2 'retained'); the orchestrator closed each terminal by hand.

FILES (yours): scripts/orca-wait.sh (process_batch's worker_done branch, after rec_mark_done), tests/orca-wait-retained.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Read tests/orca-wait.bats and tests/orca-wait-records.bats first and reuse their stub-orca fixture; do not edit them. Base = main at 1c18272 (has claude-orca-20o's rec_mark_done).

SPEC
1. On worker_done without --keep: after worker-release, if the release answer's .result.state is not one of released|closed|gone (e.g. "retained"), call `orca terminal close --terminal <handle>` for the dispatch record's terminal (orca_call terminal close ...). Note the line "closed <terminal> (worker-release left it retained)". released=true in the record only when the release state was terminal OR the close succeeded; otherwise released=false and a note.
2. With --keep: never close.
3. The receipt JSON gains "terminal_closed": true|false.

CONTRACT
CHECK: bats tests/orca-wait-retained.bats
PASS-IF: plan 1..N, N>=3, no 'not ok'. Cases: (1) stub orca answers worker-release with {"result":{"state":"retained"}} -> the stub's call log shows `terminal close --terminal term_x1`, the receipt has terminal_closed true and released true, the record has released true; (2) --keep -> no terminal close in the call log, terminal_closed false; (3) worker-release answers state "released" -> no terminal close, released true, terminal_closed false; (4) tests/orca-wait.bats and tests/orca-wait-records.bats stay green.

description:

A Claude worker is stopped by the PreToolUse contract-gate hook (config/claude-settings.json); an opencode/codex/gemini worker runs none of this repo's hooks, so FROZEN is enforced by spec text alone. Enforce it in git instead, for every agent.

FILES (yours): scripts/lib/frozen-hook.sh (NEW: the pre-commit hook body + an installer function), scripts/orca-dispatch.sh (install the hook into the worktree it dispatches into, right after the worktree is resolved and before worker-start), scripts/delegate.sh (same, into the job worktree), tests/frozen-hook.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Do not edit scripts/orca-wait.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, tests/orca-dispatch*.bats, tests/delegate.bats. Base = main at 1c18272.

SPEC
1. The hook (installed as <worktree>/.git/hooks/pre-commit, or for a linked worktree at $(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-commit; do not clobber a user hook: if one exists and is not ours, chain it by renaming to pre-commit.orig and calling it first) reads the bead id from the env var CLAUDE_ORCA_BEAD or from a file <git-path>/claude-orca-bead written by the installer, runs `bd show <bead>` (BEADS_DIR from the environment as usual), extracts the FROZEN paths (the line(s) starting with 'FROZEN:' -- paths are the tokens ending in .bats/.sh/.py/.js/.md before the word 'from') and the RED-AT sha (a note matching 'RED-AT[:=] *<sha>' or a commit whose subject starts with 'RED:' and mentions the bead). If a RED-AT exists in this repo's history and the staged diff touches any FROZEN path, the hook exits 1 printing: "frozen: <path> is frozen from <sha> (<bead>); do not commit changes to it -- if the test is wrong, run: bd supersede <bead>". Otherwise exit 0. No bd on PATH, no bead, or bd failure -> exit 0 (never block a commit on tooling).
2. Installer: install_frozen_hook <worktree-dir> <bead-id>; idempotent; bash 3.2-clean is NOT required (container-only) but keep it POSIX-ish.
3. orca-dispatch and delegate call the installer with the bead id (delegate: only for --bead jobs).

title: Orca-launched Claude workers die on the 'Bypass Permissions mode' acceptance dialog (worker-start state=failed)
description:
Seen 2026-09-17 02:29-02:40: five orca-dispatch --agent claude --model sonnet launches (beads claude-orca-gh9, claude-orca-m57) came back state=failed. The terminal shows `claude '--dangerously-skip-permissions' '--model' 'sonnet'` stopped on "WARNING: Claude Code running in Bypass Permissions mode ... ❯ No, exit / Yes, I accept" and then the shell prompt: the dialog defaults to exit and Orca's worker-start sees the process die. The same launch worked at 23:26 the previous evening (ctx_41f201d7a2fe, ctx_901477575758). Setting .bypassPermissionsModeAccepted=true in /home/agent/.claude.json did NOT help (it was null before; still fails after), so either the worker runs with a different HOME/config dir or the acceptance lives under another key in this Claude Code version.
To do: find where Claude Code 2.x records the acceptance (grep the installed claude bundle for 'bypassPermissionsModeAccepted' / 'Bypass Permissions' and the settings key it reads; check what HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Orca's worker-start gives the terminal, e.g. via `orca terminal create --command 'env | grep -E \"HOME|CLAUDE\"'`), seed it at provision time (scripts/container/provision.d/, the step that seeds the agent home) so a fresh folder never shows the dialog to a worker, and add a bats case. Until then Sonnet slices go through the Agent tool (which is what happened here).
notes:
Root cause: Claude Code 2.1.271 migrated ~/.claude.json's bypassPermissionsModeAccepted into settings.json's skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt (userSettings/localSettings/flagSettings/policySettings), deleting the old key once migrated (grep -o '.{80}bypassPermissionsModeAccepted.{80}' on the installed bundle shows migration fn 'yi'). provision.d/30-claude-first-run already seeds the new key once, but config-sync.sh's settings.json rewrite is a wholesale overwrite from the template and runs again independently later (host resync / /config-resync) without 30 re-running after it, so the seeded key gets wiped and the interactive Bypass Permissions dialog reappears -- matching the incident timeline (worked at 23:26, failed 02:29-02:40 after an intervening resync).

Repo fix (branch joe-rayment/wt-bypass-accept, commit 7960a77): config/claude-settings.json now ships skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true so every config-sync rewrite carries it, not just the first; settings.local.json still overrides. Added a bats case to tests/config-sync.bats proving the key survives a forced second sync and that a local override still wins (RED: null after first sync pre-fix; GREEN: true after first AND forced second sync post-fix, false with a local override). ./run-tests.sh: 58 files, 4 pre-existing not-ok unrelated to this change (opencode config sync test, start-professor cwd test, statusline legacy-fixture test, opencode-dispatch guard-token test) -- reproduce identically without this diff.

LIVE change in this container (not just the worktree): added "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true to /home/agent/.claude/settings.json directly, so orca-dispatch --agent claude works now without waiting for a fresh provision run. Reproduced before/after via orca terminal create: before the live edit, 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model sonnet' (interactive, no -p) stopped on the WARNING/Bypass Permissions dialog defaulting to 'No, exit'; after the edit, the same command landed straight in the REPL and answered a prompt (Crunched for 1s, turn completed) with no dialog.
close_reason: Root cause: config-sync rewrote settings.json without skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt (Claude Code 2.1.271 moved the acceptance there). Fixed in config/claude-settings.json with a config-sync.bats case; merged at 1daaaf4; live settings patched; a Sonnet worker then launched cleanly on Orca (claude-orca-cgq).

title: orca-dispatch's opencode worker blocks on an interactive permission dialog (external_directory /tmp) that nobody can answer
description:
OBJECTIVE
Seen 2026-09-17, bead claude-orca-bvm on the GLM 5.3 flash worker: the opencode TUI launched by orca-dispatch (scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh orca_opencode_command -> `opencode --model ...`) stopped for 10+ minutes on "△ Permission required ← Access external directory /tmp  Allow once / Allow always / Reject". A dispatched worker has nobody at the keyboard, so every opencode 'ask' is a silent stall. The batch path (scripts/delegate.sh) already runs `opencode run --auto`; the TUI path has no equivalent flag, but opencode's config has one (https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/): top-level "permission": "allow" or a granular object {"*":"allow","bash":{"*":"allow","git push *":"deny"}}; external_directory and doom_loop default to "ask".

FILES (yours): scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh (orca_opencode_command), tests/opencode-permissions.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Do not touch scripts/orca-wait.sh, scripts/delegate.sh, scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, tests/variant-carry.bats (frozen) -- but read tests/variant-carry.bats cases 1-4 first: they pin today's shape (no variant + no token -> the bare command and NO files) and must stay green, so the permission block is added WITHOUT changing the bare-command case. Achieve that by keeping the bare case bare only when... no: the contract below changes the bare case, so instead extend variant-carry's frozen expectations? NO -- frozen. Resolution: the permission block goes into the SAME per-launch config file, and the config file is now written on EVERY launch; variant-carry case 3 ("no variant, no token -> exactly `opencode --model ...` and no files") will therefore fail. Check: run `bats tests/variant-carry.bats` at the start; if case 3 asserts 'no files', report that conflict in your first heartbeat and implement this instead: write the permission-only config to <run_dir>/opencode-launch/permissions.json ONLY when CLAUDE_ORCA_OPENCODE_PERMISSIONS is not "ask" (default "allow"), and make the bare-command case (variant-carry 3) keep passing by treating CLAUDE_ORCA_OPENCODE_PERMISSIONS=ask as the no-file path in that test's environment -- i.e. the new test sets nothing and expects the file, variant-carry sets nothing and expects no file: these conflict. Therefore the ONLY clean answer: the new bats file and this change must ALSO bump tests/variant-carry.bats case 3 -- which is frozen under a CLOSED bead (claude-orca-y0y); a closed bead's frozen test may be updated by a later contract that deliberately changes the shape (coordinator rule, see tests/delegate.bats precedent in commit 8d53a50). Make that one-case edit (case 3 becomes: no variant, no token -> command sources an env file whose OPENCODE_CONFIG names a file with permission but with no models block and no baseURL), list it as a deviation.

SPEC
1. orca_opencode_command ALWAYS writes the per-launch config and env file. The config carries: "permission": {"*": "allow", "bash": {"*": "allow", "git push *": "deny", "git push": "deny"}, "external_directory": {"*": "allow"}} (exact keys; opencode merges), plus the existing provider block (baseURL/apiKey only with a guard token; models.<id>.options.reasoning.effort only with a variant). CLAUDE_ORCA_OPENCODE_PERMISSIONS=ask disables the permission block (config still written).
2. The printed command keeps the `set -a; . '<env>'; set +a; opencode --model <m>` shape in every case.

CONTRACT
CHECK: bats tests/opencode-permissions.bats
PASS-IF: plan 1..N with N>=4, no 'not ok'. Cases: (1) no variant, no token -> command sources an env file; OPENCODE_CONFIG names a file whose .permission["*"]=="allow", .permission.bash["git push *"]=="deny", .permission.external_directory["*"]=="allow", and which has no .provider.openrouter.models and no baseURL; (2) with variant high and a token -> the same permission block AND models.<id>.options.reasoning.effort=="high" AND baseURL; (3) CLAUDE_ORCA_OPENCODE_PERMISSIONS=ask -> config has no .permission key; (4) `bats tests/variant-carry.bats` green after the one-case edit; (5) config mode 600.
FROZEN: tests/opencode-permissions.bats from RED-AT on.
CLASS: bugfix.

PROCESS: RED commit (test file only; note RED-AT), implement, GREEN commit (note GREEN-AT). Keep bats tests/orca-dispatch-launch.bats tests/orca-dispatch.bats green. Report under 60 lines with the variant-carry deviation called out.

title: orca-wait: a finished dispatch stays 'ready' in its record, so the stall watch nudges dead workers and ends a live wait
description:
OBJECTIVE
Seen 2026-09-17: orca-wait, waiting on a LIVE recon dispatch (ctx_2c2eecfc6de4), printed "ctx_41f201d7a2fe (claude-orca-2j2) is still quiet 7538s after its nudge -- falling back to an in-process executor" and exited 0 -- for a dispatch whose worker_done had been ingested and whose terminal had been released two hours earlier (bead closed). Cause: process_batch (scripts/orca-wait.sh) on worker_done notes the bead and calls worker-release, but never updates the dispatch RECORD (.claude-dev/run/orchestration/dispatch/<id>.json, written by orca-dispatch, shape in scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh header), so state stays "ready"; stall_scan scans every record in ready/running/dispatched, nudges the dead terminal, and on the next pass returns 3, which ends the whole wait. Records from Sep 12 and Sep 16 are still "ready" today.

FILES (yours): scripts/orca-wait.sh, tests/orca-wait-records.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Read tests/orca-wait.bats first for the stub-orca and fixture pattern and reuse it. Do not touch scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh or tests/orca-wait.bats.

SPEC
1. On worker_done (and on the release it performs), process_batch writes the record: .state = "done", .outcome = <outcome or "unknown">, .finished_at = <epoch>, .released = true|false (true when worker-release succeeded). On question/escalation the record is only touched (rec_touch), as today.
2. stall_scan skips any record whose state is not ready/running/dispatched (already so) AND any record whose bead is closed: `bd show <bead> --json` status closed (use orch_bead_json if it exposes status; else jq on its output) -> mark that record .state = "done" .finished_at = now with a note "<disp> (<bead>): bead is closed -- marking the dispatch done" and continue. A failed bd lookup leaves the record alone.
3. The nudged-again fallback (return 3) must not end a wait when another dispatch in the same run is still live: instead of `return 3`, mark that record .state = "stalled" (so it is scanned no more), print the same {"type":"stalled",...,"fallback":...} line, and return 3 ONLY if no other record in $DISP_DIR is in ready/running/dispatched state; otherwise return 0 and keep waiting.
4. A `--keep` wait (no release) still marks the record done with released=false.

CONTRACT
CHECK: bats tests/orca-wait-records.bats
PASS-IF: plan 1..N with N>=5, no 'not ok'. Cases: (1) a stub `orca` that answers one worker_done for dispatch X: after orca-wait, X's record has state "done", outcome from the payload, finished_at > 0, released true; (2) same with --keep: state "done", released false; (3) a record for dispatch Y with state "ready", nudged_at set, activity 2h old, while a record Z is "ready" and fresh: orca-wait with --stall-after 60 and a stub whose check --wait returns count 0 prints one stalled line with fallback for Y, sets Y's state to "stalled", and does NOT exit until its --timeout-ms (assert it printed the {"type":"timeout"} line and Z is still "ready"); (4) the same Y alone (no Z): orca-wait exits after the fallback line without the timeout line (today's behaviour, kept); (5) a record whose bead the stub `bd` reports closed: never nudged (stub orca records no `terminal send`), record marked done with a note; (6) existing `bats tests/orca-wait.bats` stays green.

CLASS: bugfix.

title: Carry the role's reasoning-effort variant into opencode: orca-dispatch, orca_opencode_command, delegate, luna route (claude-orca-1w8 slice B)
description:
OBJECTIVE
A role bound with an effort (roles.<role>.variant in .claude-dev/run/tier.json, e.g. recon = openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna @high) must actually run at that effort when the slice is dispatched to opencode, on BOTH paths: the Orca terminal path (orca-dispatch -> orca_opencode_command -> `opencode --model ...` TUI) and the batch path (bin/delegate run -> `opencode run`). Verified in this container on opencode 1.18.25 (2026-09-16): the TUI has NO --variant flag, but a config file naming `provider.openrouter.models.<vendor/model>.options.reasoning.effort = "high"` turns reasoning tokens on for openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna (0 -> 13 on a trivial prompt; the key `reasoningEffort` does NOT work), and opencode honours the OPENCODE_CONFIG env var pointing at that file. Use that one mechanism for both paths.
The shared helper is already in (commit a46070f): scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh `tier_role_field <state> <role> variant`, tier_role_label shows @<variant>.

FILES (yours): scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh (orca_opencode_command), scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/delegate.sh, scripts/tier-gate.sh (note text only), config/delegate-routes.json, tests/variant-carry.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Do NOT touch scripts/tier-set.sh, scripts/tier-prime.sh, scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh, config/claude-commands/tier.md (another slice owns them).

Change: whenever a variant is given OR a guard token exists, write a per-launch config <run_dir>/opencode-launch/<slug>.json (slug = model with / and : replaced by -, plus -<variant> when set; mode 600; mkdir -p) containing {"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json","provider":{"openrouter":{"options":{apiKey:"{env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", baseURL:<guard url>} -- only when the token exists --,"models":{"<vendor/model>":{"options":{"reasoning":{"effort":"<variant>"}}}}}}} (the models block only when a variant is set; <vendor/model> is the id with the leading `openrouter/` stripped), and add `OPENCODE_CONFIG='<that file>'` to the env file (the env file is written in every case that has a config; without a token it carries only OPENCODE_CONFIG). The printed command keeps the `set -a; . <env>; set +a; opencode --model <m>` shape. No variant and no token -> unchanged bare command, no files.
2. orca-dispatch: new flag `--variant <e>`; default = tier_role_field "$STATE_FILE" "$ROLE" variant; passed as the 3rd arg to orca_opencode_command on the opencode path; recorded as `variant` in the dispatch record JSON and the receipt line (`variant=<e|none>`). title: tier-set: positional/per-role phrases with short names, catalogue lookup and @effort (claude-orca-1w8 slice A)
description:
OBJECTIVE
/tier must accept a trio like `fable glm-flash luna@high` or `fable, GLM 5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)` (POSITIONAL order: top, worker, recon) and per-role forms like `recon luna high`, resolve the names, and record a reasoning-effort variant per role. Today tier-set's positional form takes only Claude aliases and nothing knows about effort. The shared helper is already in: scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh (commit a46070f) prints a 5th column `variant` from roles.<role>.variant, tier_role_field accepts `variant`, tier_role_label appends `@<variant>`.

FILES (yours): scripts/tier-set.sh, scripts/tier-prime.sh, config/claude-commands/tier.md, tests/tier-phrases.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Do NOT touch scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh, scripts/delegate.sh, scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, config/delegate-routes.json (another slice owns them).

SPEC
1. Argument normalisation, first thing in tier-set: when invoked with exactly ONE argument that contains a comma or whitespace, re-split it -- on commas when any are present (each phrase trimmed), else on whitespace -- and continue as if those were the args. An empty single argument behaves like no args (show). tier.md changes its one line to `!`tier-set "$ARGUMENTS"`` so commas/parentheses survive the shell, and its argument-hint documents the new forms (examples below). Keep tier.md a verbatim passthrough.
2. `help`, `-h`, `--help` print the explanation and bind NOTHING (today `tier-set --help` binds top=--help). Any positional token starting with `-` is rejected with a usage error, nothing bound.
3. Effort words: none minimal low medium high xhigh max. A phrase carries one as `<name>@<e>`, `<name> (<e>)` / `<name>(<e>)`, or a trailing bare word `<name> <e>` (whitespace inside a comma phrase, or the 3rd token of the per-role form `tier-set recon luna high`). Anything else after `@` is an error.
4. Resolution of a worker/recon phrase (a function, reused by positional and per-role forms), yielding backend/agent/model:
   a. Claude aliases fable|opus|sonnet|haiku (any case) and full claude-* ids -> as today (positional: write_state's rules; per-role: subagent/claude pinned).
   b. Existing specs unchanged: openrouter:<vendor/model>, openrouter, claude:<x>, codex:<id>, gemini:<id>, orca, subagent, inherit. `openrouter:<vendor/model>@high` works.
   c. A route NAME from config/delegate-routes.json (path overridable by TIER_ROUTES_FILE; default = <repo>/config/delegate-routes.json resolved via lib/paths.sh like tier-set finds tier-derive) resolves to that route's `.model` (e.g. glm-flash -> openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash) with backend orca, agent opencode, pinned true.
   d. A phrase containing `/` is an explicit OpenRouter id (a leading `openrouter/` is optional and normalised in): bound as typed, backend orca, agent opencode.
   e. Anything else is looked up in the catalogue: TIER_MODELS_FILE (default <run dir>/openrouter-models.json, i.e. next to tier.json) holding the raw JSON of GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (public, no key). Fetch with curl -m 10 when the file is absent or older than 24h unless TIER_MODELS_FETCH=0; a failed fetch keeps any existing file. Matching: lowercase the query, split on whitespace, strip every non [a-z0-9] char from each word; a model matches when every word is a substring of the concatenation of its normalised id and name. Ids containing ':' (batch/free/exacto variants) are excluded unless the query itself contains ':'. Exactly one match -> bind it. Several, where one id is a prefix of every other -> bind that one (so "gpt-5.6 luna" beats luna-pro). Otherwise print up to 10 candidates as `<id>  <name>  $<prompt>/$<completion> per M` and exit 1 with "nothing bound". No catalogue and no fetch -> exit 1 saying so and suggesting the explicit vendor/model form.
5. `tier-set models [<words>]` prints the candidates for <words> (same matcher, no prefix rule, all shown) or, with no words, the ids of every route in delegate-routes.json plus the catalogue count/age. Exit 0.
6. State: positional `tier-set <top> <worker> [<recon>]` still writes top/worker/recon and pinned=true; for an OpenRouter worker/recon the role block becomes {backend: orca, agent: opencode, model: openrouter/<vendor/model>, pinned: true, variant: <e>} (variant key absent when none). A Claude role with an effort prints `tier: effort '<e>' applies to OpenRouter roles only -- ignored for <role>` and binds the model. Per-role form writes the same block via write_role (extend it to take an optional variant). Top stays a Claude alias/id; an effort on top is ignored with the same note.
7. Output: the bound lines use tier_role_label (which now shows @variant). tier-prime passes the 5th column into tier_role_label so the SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit lines read e.g. `worker=orca:opencode:openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash recon=orca:opencode:openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna@high`.
8. Examples for tier.md's argument-hint: `fable glm-flash luna@high` | `fable, GLM 5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)` | `fable z-ai/glm-5.3-flash openai/gpt-5.6-luna@high` | `recon luna high` | `worker openrouter:qwen/qwen3-coder` | `models luna`.

TEST FIXTURES: tests/tier-phrases.bats uses TIER_STATE_FILE, TIER_SETTINGS_LOCAL, TIER_DERIVE (see tests/tier-hooks.bats for the pattern), TIER_ROUTES_FILE pointing at a fixture routes json with glm-flash and luna, TIER_MODELS_FILE pointing at a fixture catalogue with at least: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:batch, z-ai/glm-5.3, openai/gpt-5.6-luna, openai/gpt-5.6-luna-pro, openai/gpt-luna-latest, sao10k/l3-lunaris-8b, each with name and pricing.prompt/completion; TIER_MODELS_FETCH=0 everywhere. No network, no real Orca (tier_orca_reachable must see nothing: unset ORCA_* or point CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT at the fixture).

CONTRACT

PASS-IF: plan 1..N with N>=11, no 'not ok'. Cases, one @test each: (1) single quoted arg "fable glm-flash luna@high" -> tier.json top=fable, roles.worker={orca,opencode,openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash,pinned true, no variant}, roles.recon={orca,opencode,openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna,variant high}, pinned=true; (2) "fable, GLM 5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)" gives the identical role blocks; (3) "fable z-ai/glm-5.3-flash openai/gpt-5.6-luna@high" identical; (4) "fable sonnet luna" -> worker subagent/claude/sonnet-style as today, recon luna no variant; (5) ambiguous "fable glm-flash luna-latest-or-lunaris"-style query (a phrase matching >=2 ids with no common prefix, e.g. "luna") prints >=2 candidate lines, exits 1, tier.json byte-identical to before; (6) "--help" and "help" exit 0, print the explanation, create/modify no state file; (7) "recon luna high" per-role -> roles.recon variant high, worker untouched; (8) "worker glm-flash@bogus" exits 1 nothing bound; (9) "fable sonnet@high haiku" binds sonnet, prints the 'applies to OpenRouter roles only' note; (10) "models luna" exits 0 and lists at least openai/gpt-5.6-luna and openai/gpt-5.6-luna-pro; (11) TIER_MODELS_FILE absent + TIER_MODELS_FETCH=0: "fable glm-flash gpt-5.6-luna" exits 1 mentioning the catalogue, while "fable glm-flash openai/gpt-5.6-luna@high" binds; (12) tier-prime --short output contains "@high" after the recon binding from (1).

title: claude-dev --teardown leaves files that block git push
description:
ORIGINAL: When running claude-dev --teardown, some files are left in the working directory that shouldn't be there. These prevent pushing the repo to a separate git remote.

RECON (claude-orca-4tm, 2026-09-17, by the recon role): after teardown the folder still holds .orca-worktrees/** (Orca's linked git worktrees, each with a .git FILE pointing into the root .git/worktrees -- `git add -A` stages them as mode-160000 embedded-repo gitlinks, which is what breaks a push to a fresh remote), root .orca/** (Orca drops), .claude-dev-snapshots/<ts>/ (the beads snapshot, by design, TEARDOWN_RECOVERY.md), attachments/, and the user's .beads/. gitignore_unseed (scripts/launcher.sh ~186-215) removes every seeded ignore line, so the survivors become visible untracked files. Neither .orca/ nor .orca-worktrees/ is in the seed block (scripts/container/provision.d/50-seed-project ~63-75), so they show as untracked during the folder's whole life too (this checkout: `?? .orca/`).

OBJECTIVE: teardown leaves no Orca residue and the seed ignores Orca's on-disk state while the folder lives. The beads snapshot and attachments stay (documented recovery data; the user decides) -- out of scope here.

FILES: scripts/launcher.sh (cmd_teardown_v3 + the unseed list; bash 3.2 -- no mapfile/assoc arrays/${x^^}; scripts/lint-bash32.sh must pass), scripts/container/provision.d/50-seed-project (the seed block), tests/teardown-orca-residue.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). title: /tier: bind OpenRouter-hosted worker/recon by name with a reasoning effort (e.g. fable, glm-5.3-flash, gpt-5.6-luna@high)
description:
WHY IT NEVER CAME THROUGH (verified 2026-09-16 in this container):
- config/claude-commands/tier.md is a verbatim shell passthrough: !`tier-set $ARGUMENTS`, model haiku, effort low, 'no analysis'. Free text like 'GLM5.3 flash' or '(high)' reaches tier-set untouched.
- tier-set's 1/2/3-arg positional form only accepts Claude ladder aliases: valid_id() forbids '/' and ':', so no openrouter id can ride there. The ONLY OpenRouter form is per-role: /tier worker openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.3-flash.
- Nothing in tier-set, tier-roles.sh, tier-gate, orca-dispatch, orca_opencode_command or bin/delegate has an effort/variant concept.
- Bug found: `tier-set --help` binds top=--help (valid_id accepts it). Restored by hand.

GROUND TRUTH:
- OpenRouter ids (from the guard's /api/v1/models): z-ai/glm-5.3-flash ($0.075/$0.25 per M), z-ai/glm-5.3 ($1.4/$4.4), openai/gpt-5.6-luna ($0.2/$1.2), openai/gpt-5.6-luna-pro, -terra, -sol; all openai/gpt-5.6-* advertise reasoning_effort.
- opencode 1.18.25: `opencode run --variant high` is a built-in variant, needs NO config; on openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna through the guard it turned reasoning tokens 0 -> 12 on a trivial prompt (cost 0.00151 -> 0.00153). Declaring variants.high.reasoning.effort in opencode.json gives the same result.
- delegate run --route glm-flash / glm work end to end through the guard (DELEGATION-OK; file written in worktree).
- The running container uses the IMAGE's entrypoint (pre-b30): no guard this boot until a restart; the guard now running was started by hand from opencode's auth.json.

PLAN (slices, each its own bead when work starts):
1. tier-set: positional worker/recon accept role specs (openrouter:<vendor/model>, claude:<alias>, subagent) and an '@<effort>' suffix (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh); stored as roles.<role>.variant in tier.json; valid_model_ref admits '@'. Reject --help/-h explicitly. Positional 'top' stays a Claude alias (the orchestrator is this session).
2. tier-set `models [<words>]`: list/fuzzy-match ids from run/openrouter-models.json (cached from the guard's /models, refreshed when the token file changes). Unknown positional tokens resolve through it: unique match binds, ambiguity prints candidates and binds nothing. Deterministic, no LLM.
3. tier.md: argument-hint + a one-line rule: if tier-set prints candidates, pick by the user's words and re-run once. Stays a passthrough otherwise.
4. Carry the variant: orca_opencode_command appends --variant <v>; bin/delegate run passes --variant when the route or tier role carries one; tier-gate notes it for orca-backed roles. An openrouter recon MUST be orca-backed (a subagent is Claude only) -- tier-set sets backend=orca for it and tier-gate's scout note says 'orca-dispatch --recon'.
5. Auth path: opencode auth login openrouter in a plain Orca terminal -> auth.json -> entrypoint (b30) starts the guard on next boot. orca_opencode_command already uses the guard token when present and falls back to direct auth.json (2c3c003 unpinned). Decide whether orca-backed opencode may bypass the guard when no token exists.
6. Tests: bats for 1/2 (parse, suffix, fuzzy, ambiguity, --help), delegate --variant passthrough.

OPEN: which role is which in 'Fable, GLM5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)': worker=glm-flash recon=luna@high (positional order), or worker=luna@high recon=glm-flash (cost order)?

Pushed to origin.

The real key already sits in auth.json today -- this reads it, it does not put it there.

title: opencode cannot connect: the guard baseURL is written even when no guard runs
description:
SYMPTOM: opencode (OpenRouter) inside the container fails every call with 'Cannot connect to API: Unable to connect'. Orca shows 'Refresh failed'.

ROOT CAUSE (verified inside the live container, 2026-09-16):
- ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json forces provider.openrouter.options.baseURL = http://127.0.0.1:4141/api/v1 (config/opencode/opencode.json:7, copied verbatim by config-sync.sh -- no conditional rewrite).
- Nothing listens on 4141: curl -> 'Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 4141'; no openrouter-guard.log / .pid / .token in .claude-dev/run; ps shows no guard.
- Why: .claude-dev/home/.openrouter.key does not exist, so container_create() (scripts/launcher.sh:2199-2204) passes no -e OPENROUTER_API_KEY; entrypoint.sh:593 then logs 'no OPENROUTER_API_KEY; not starting the OpenRouter guard' and fails closed by design.
- So the request never reaches openrouter.ai. ECONNREFUSED on loopback is what opencode reports as 'Unable to connect'.

NOT the cause: outbound HTTPS to openrouter.ai is HTTP/2 200 from inside; the IPv6/Bun hypothesis is moot because no DNS name is resolved at all.

THE GAP: the folder reports HEALTHY while opencode is unusable -- provision.d/70-openrouter-guard exits 0 with 'nothing to guard', and --doctor prints the openrouter key row as n/a. A folder whose synced client config points at a guard that is not running is broken, and must say so.

title: seed-project: never write through an orca.yaml symlink (supersedes claude-orca-8jb)
description:
claude-orca-8jb's verification found one defect in the new seed_orca_yaml() migration.

The same idempotent script runs twice, and one of those runs is deliberately visible.

    and orca.yaml's own seeded comment says it plainly: "scripts.setup runs in a terminal when a workspace is created, so the work below is watchable". That terminal is the second tab, and what it runs is the SAME seeding that provisioning has already done.

The "watchable" rationale predates provision.d. Provisioning now gives every step a log and a status row that `provision status` and the SessionStart hook read back, so the visible terminal buys nothing and costs the user a tab on every workspace.

title: provision: orchestration-skill install decides by exact name only, --json authoritative (supersedes claude-orca-4gx)
description:
Supersedes claude-orca-4gx (which superseded claude-orca-ndy). Same goal. Third contract; the first two both shipped a wrongful-skip hole, so the cases below are written to close the CLASS, not the instance.

THE BUG CLASS, stated once: this step decides whether to install by reading text. Every version so far has decided "already installed" from a word appearing somewhere in that text. When it guesses wrong in that direction, `skills install` never runs, the step exits 0, and `provision status` shows a green row — the user's "Orchestration: Not Installed" persists forever with the provisioning system reporting success. A wrongful SKIP is invisible and permanent. A wrongful INSTALL costs one idempotent network call. The step must be biased to install whenever it is not certain.

WHAT 4gx STILL GOT WRONG (verifier, reproduced against the real step):
  (b) --json unsupported, a flush-left prose line "pairs with the orchestration skill" -> SKIPPED. Wrong.
  (d) plain output carrying "warning: orchestration index stale" -> SKIPPED. Wrong.
4gx's fallback drops indented lines, then whole-token matches anywhere in what survives:
    grep -v -E '^[[:space:]]' | grep -qE '(^|[[:space:]])orchestration([[:space:]]|\(|$)'
Indentation is the only thing separating a name from prose there, and the token match floats anywhere in the line. Wrapped prose, a warning, or any flush-left diagnostic reopens the exact hole.
Correct in 4gx and to be preserved: (a) indented prose -> installs; (c) a skill named `orchestration-extras` -> installs (hyphen is not a boundary).

THE FIX, two parts.

1. Make --json AUTHORITATIVE. Today a confident --json "not installed" still falls through to the fuzzy fallback, which can then overrule it. It must not. Decide in this order:
   - run `"$cli" skills installed --json`; if it exits 0 AND its output PARSES as JSON (e.g. `jq -e . >/dev/null`), that answer is final: installed iff `jq -e '.result.skills[] | select(.name == "orchestration")'` matches. Never consult the plain path afterward, in either direction.
   - otherwise (non-zero exit, unparseable output, or no jq) fall through to 2.
   This alone kills (d): a zero exit carrying non-JSON no longer counts as authoritative, and no longer silently lands in the fuzzy path with its hole intact.

2. ANCHOR the fallback to the start of the line. A selector line begins with the name. Prose, warnings and locations do not:
       grep -qE '^orchestration([[:space:]]|\(|$)'
   ndy's frozen case-2 fixture prints one flush-left space-separated list of bare names ("beads orchestration snowpark-deploy"), where orchestration is not first — handle that as a SEPARATE, explicit alternative (e.g. a line consisting only of bare names, no parens and no prose punctuation, matched token-wise), not by loosening the anchor for everything. If that degenerate shape cannot be discriminated cleanly from prose, prefer INSTALLING over skipping and say so in your report — case 2's fixture predates the real two-line format and is the weakest thing in this contract.

Unchanged from 4gx and still required: `skills install --skill orchestration --local` (never drop --local -- bare default installs GLOBALLY across every project on the host); non-fatal but honest non-zero exit when install fails; exit 0 with a log line when no CLI resolves; default to attempting the install when nothing is confident.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/provision-orca-skills.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N, no 'not ok'
FROZEN: tests/provision-orca-skills.bats (re-frozen at this bead's RED-AT)

  9.  --json unsupported; plain output has NO orchestration selector but a FLUSH-LEFT prose line mentioning "orchestration" -> MUST INSTALL. (verifier probe (b))
  10. --json unsupported; plain output has NO orchestration selector but a flush-left line "warning: orchestration index stale" -> MUST INSTALL. (verifier probe (d))
  11. `--json` exits 0 but prints non-JSON garbage; no orchestration installed -> MUST INSTALL. (the authoritativeness hole)
  12. `--json` exits 0 with VALID JSON listing orchestration as installed, while the plain output does NOT mention it at all -> MUST NOT INSTALL (json is authoritative in the positive direction).
  13. `--json` exits 0 with VALID JSON that does NOT list orchestration, while the plain output DOES contain a flush-left line mentioning orchestration -> MUST INSTALL (json authoritative in the negative direction; the fallback must never overrule it).

BOUNDARIES

title: provision: install the orchestration skill with an EXACT installed-check (supersedes claude-orca-ndy)
description:
Supersedes claude-orca-ndy. Same goal, contract widened by one case that ndy's frozen tests could not catch.

WHY ndy FAILED VERIFICATION. Its step checked idempotency like this:

    installed="$("$cli" skills installed 2>/dev/null)"
    case "$installed" in
        *orchestration*) echo "already installed"; exit 0 ;;
    esac

That is an unanchored substring match over the ENTIRE stdout of `orca skills installed`, which prints a two-line record per skill -- a `name (hash)` selector line AND an indented prose description, plus a location line. Orca's bundled skill descriptions cross-reference each other by name ("Use `orca-cli` instead for...", "pairs with the orchestration skill..."), so a skill that is NOT orchestration can carry the word "orchestration" in its description and satisfy the match.

Reproduced by the verifier against the real step with a stub emitting the real format (beads + snowpark-deploy installed, NO orchestration selector, snowpark-deploy's description mentioning "the orchestration skill"):

    the orchestration skill is already installed; nothing to do
    step exit=0
    --- install log ---
    (end log)

`skills install` never ran, the step exited 0, and `provision status` records a green row. The user's symptom -- Settings showing "Orchestration: Not Installed" -- would persist silently on every boot forever, with the provisioning system actively reporting success. That failure mode is worse than the original bug, because it is invisible.

ndy's four frozen cases do not cover it: its "already installed" fixture puts `orchestration` in a selector position, so selector-vs-description is never discriminated.

  - fallback, when jq is missing or --json is unsupported by an older Orca: anchor to the selector line's real shape, `grep -qE '^orchestration \('` -- start of line, name, space, open paren. Never a bare substring over the whole output.
  - if BOTH paths are unavailable/inconclusive, prefer attempting the install over skipping it. `skills install` is itself idempotent (npx skills add re-resolves), so a redundant install costs a network call; a wrongful skip costs the entire feature, silently. Bias toward the recoverable error.

title: claude-dev --update installs the newest Claude Code, not a hand-set pin
description:
USER REQUEST (asked three times, 2026-09-14): --update must get the LATEST Claude Code, not whatever literal a human last typed into the pin.

Today the pin is a literal in three lockstep files and a rebuild can only ever install that literal. Worse, the payload layer keys on the ARG value, so when the literal does not change Docker reuses the cached layer and the install step never re-runs (observed: /opt/claude/claude dated 2026-09-12 21:45 surviving a 2026-09-14 22:03 rebuild).

GROUND TRUTH established this session:
  https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest -> '2.1.271', 7 bytes,
  no trailing newline, content-type text/plain, cache-control no-cache max-age=0.
  A sibling 'stable' pointer returns 2.1.236. npm dist-tags agree
  (stable=2.1.236, latest=2.1.271). curl -f exits 22 on a bad path.
  The resolved version always has a <version>/manifest.json carrying linux-arm64.

DESIGN (decided, not open):
  Resolution happens OUTSIDE the docker build and arrives as
  --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=<resolved>, reusing the ARG plumbing that
  already exists. Resolving INSIDE a RUN layer would be cached forever and
  reproduce the exact bug being fixed. When a new release ships the ARG value
  changes and the layer cache busts by itself; when nothing shipped the cache
  hits and the build stays fast.
  The existing literal stops being 'the version' and becomes the FALLBACK
  floor: offline, DNS-blocked or garbage response falls back to it and the
  build still succeeds. A build must never fail over a network blip.
  CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_VERSION=<x.y.z> forces an exact version and skips the
  network -- the rollback path, since 'always latest' otherwise removes the
  user's ability to escape a bad release.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/claude-version-resolve.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N with no 'not ok' line and one 'ok' per case
FROZEN: tests/claude-version-resolve.bats
Cases the contract requires:
  1. a stubbed 200 returning '2.1.271' resolves to exactly 2.1.271
  2. a stubbed curl failure (exit 22) falls back to the literal pin, exit 0
  3. a non-semver body (an HTML error page) is REJECTED and falls back --
     never passed through to a build-arg
  4. CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_VERSION=9.9.9 wins and makes no network call
  5. the resolver never prints an empty string
  6. the launcher's docker build call passes --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=
  7. scripts/lint-bash32.sh stays clean (host-side code is bash 3.2)

NOTE: tests/container-entrypoint.bats case 8 currently asserts the pin
lockstep ('ONE Claude Code pin in this repo'). Its premise is what the user
is deliberately changing, so that case legitimately changes meaning -- say so
in the commit rather than quietly editing it green.

Touches the Dockerfile and scripts/container/, so per CLAUDE.md the definition
of done needs tests/mac-e2e.sh on a real Mac; none here, so UNVERIFIED.
close_reason:
GREEN-AT-2 f2c170e, verifier PASS, pushed as 3c055a6. Host-side proof carried by claude-orca-y6q.

--update now resolves the newest Claude Code outside the docker build and passes it as --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION, so the ARG value changes when a release ships and the payload layer cache busts by itself. Resolving inside a RUN layer would have been cached forever, reproducing the bug this fixes.

Shipped: scripts/resolve-claude-version.sh (never empty, always exit 0, semver-validated, falls back to the 2.1.271 floor offline or on a garbage body); launcher.sh try_build passes the arg unconditionally, guarded so a missing resolver degrades to the Dockerfile default instead of killing the build under set -e; setup.sh phase_claude resolves lazily only when no version was given, keeping the existing manifest+sha256 verification; --check no longer demands exact equality against a re-resolved latest, which would have spuriously failed 10-toolchain-verify a day after any build.

Two defects caught in review, both measured rather than argued:
 - the first cut made the build-arg conditional on differing from the Dockerfile default, green only while latest happened to equal the baked default. CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_VERSION=9.9.9 turned launcher-v3-build case 11 red, proving it would fail on the next upstream release. Fixed by passing unconditionally and narrowing that case to its documented intent.
 - it also made the suite hit the live network: one test went 1s to 11.3s against a blackholed endpoint. Fixed via the escape hatch in the shared bats setup; blackholed and clean runs now 22.89s vs 22.96s.

Verifier evidence: frozen diff empty since RED-AT; RED-AT genuinely red 7 of 8; 1..8 green at HEAD; inversion proves cases 1-4 exercise curl for real (they go red under a forced version); ./run-tests.sh 0 failures across 51 files; container suites byte-identical to b9d68b2.

Lockstep held: the container-image and container-entrypoint pin assertions stayed green untouched, since all literals still match. That contract now governs the fallback floor rather than the installed version.

title: provision: initialise a folder that is not a git repository, or has no commits, on main with a seed commit before orca repo add (Orca needs a base branch)
description:
PROBLEM. A folder bootstrapped with claude_orca shows up in the Orca app as a project with no workspace, and "Create worktree" fails with "No base branch found". Reproduced 2026-09-13 in an isolated Orca 1.4.197 runtime: `orca repo add` REJECTS a non-git folder ("Not a valid git repository"), ACCEPTS a `git init`ed repo with no commits (kind git, a main worktree listed) but every `worktree create` then throws "Could not resolve a default base ref for this repo" (the app renders that as "No base branch found"); a repo with one commit on main or master works with no remote at all. Orca resolves the base from origin/HEAD, origin/main, origin/master, refs/heads/main, refs/heads/master and nothing else. Nothing in bootstrap.sh, launcher.sh, entrypoint.sh or provision.d ever runs `git init` or a first commit in PROJECT_DIR.

OBJECTIVE. Add ONE provision step, scripts/container/provision.d/55-git-init (runs after 50-seed-project, before 60-orca-repo-add), that guarantees PROJECT_DIR is a git repository with at least one commit on a branch Orca can base a worktree on, plus its bats file, plus two doc sentences. bash 3.2 clean (no mapfile, no [[ ]] in tests, no ${x^^}, no += onto empty arrays under set -u). Source ../provision-lib.sh like the sibling steps; `set -uo pipefail`; header comment in the house style (why it exists, what it never does).

BEHAVIOUR of 55-git-init (PROJECT_DIR from provision-lib.sh; exit 1 with a message when it is not a directory or git is not on PATH):
1. inside="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>&1)".
   a. inside = true: top="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel)" compared with "$(cd "$PROJECT_DIR" && pwd -P)".
      - HEAD has commits (`git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`): print "<dir> is a git repository with commits on <branch>; nothing to do" (name the toplevel when it is a parent folder) and exit 0.
      - HEAD unborn and toplevel == PROJECT_DIR: b="$(git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD)"; if b is neither main nor master, `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main` and print that the unborn HEAD was moved from '<b>' to main because Orca only bases worktrees on main/master. Then the seed commit (step 2).
      - HEAD unborn and toplevel is a PARENT folder: print "inside the repository at <top>, which has no commits; not touching a repository that is not this folder's" and exit 1.
   b. inside != true and "$PROJECT_DIR/.git" exists: git could not read the repository (dubious ownership, corruption): print "git cannot read the repository at <dir>: <git's message verbatim>" and exit 1. NEVER run git init here.
   c. inside != true and no .git: `git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" init -q -b main` (fallback for an old git: `git init -q` then `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main`); print "initialised <dir> as a git repository on main". Then the seed commit.
2. Seed commit, in PROJECT_DIR, ONLY the seeds and never the user's files: for p in .gitignore orca.yaml .beads: skip if absent; `git add -- "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` (a .beads whose files are all ignored must not abort); keep p in the pathspec list only if `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$p"` succeeds. Identity: name="$(git config user.name 2>/dev/null || true)", email likewise; when empty use claude_orca / claude_orca@localhost via `-c user.name=... -c user.email=...` (never override a configured identity). Always `-c commit.gpgsign=false --no-verify` (bd installs hooks; no key in the container). If the pathspec list is empty: `git commit -q --allow-empty -m "$msg"`; else `git commit -q -m "$msg" -- $paths` (the pathspec form commits ONLY those paths even when the user has other files staged). msg = "claude_orca: seed commit (<paths>)" or "claude_orca: seed commit (empty)". Print "seed commit <short sha> on <branch>: <paths>". Exit 0. Idempotent: the second run takes branch 1a and does nothing.

TESTS. New tests/provision-git-init.bats (`load helpers/setup`, assertions with [ ] and functions, fixtures under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, run the step as `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$h" PROJECT_DIR="$d" bash "$STEP"` with HOME a fresh empty dir unless the case seeds a .gitconfig, and unset GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_*). Cases, one @test each:
 1 plain folder with a user file data.csv and pre-written .gitignore + orca.yaml: .git exists, HEAD is main, exactly one commit, `git ls-files` is exactly .gitignore and orca.yaml, `git status --porcelain` shows `?? data.csv`, output contains "initialised".
 2 unborn repo on master: the commit lands on master, no rename.
 3 unborn repo on trunk: HEAD is main afterwards and the output says it was moved.
 4 repo with commits: HEAD sha unchanged, output contains "nothing to do", exit 0.
 5 idempotence: two runs on a plain folder leave exactly one commit; the second output says nothing to do.
 6 identity: with no gitconfig the author email is claude_orca@localhost; with HOME/.gitconfig naming Jo <jo@example.com> the author is that.
 7 no seeds at all: an empty commit is made (one commit, `git ls-files` empty).
 8 unborn repo with the user's own file already staged: after the step the seed commit's tree (`git ls-tree --name-only HEAD`) holds only the seeds and `git diff --cached --name-only` still lists the user's file. If git refuses the pathspec form on a root commit, report that deviation in your result instead of changing the test.
 9 a subfolder of a repo with commits: exit 0, "nothing to do", no nested .git created.
 10 a .git git cannot read: run with GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 on an unborn repo: exit 1, output contains git's dubious-ownership message, no commit made.
 11 the step file is executable and `ls provision.d | sort` lists 55-git-init before 60-orca-repo-add and after 50-seed-project.
 12 a .beads directory seeded like bd init (config.yaml, issues.jsonl, and a .beads/.gitignore ignoring dolt/) is committed minus the ignored parts.
Then run `bats tests/provision-git-init.bats tests/provision.bats tests/seed-project.bats tests/container-entrypoint.bats tests/container-entrypoint-seed.bats` and `bash scripts/lint-bash32.sh` if it accepts container paths; report the TAP plan lines and every 'not ok' verbatim.

DOCS. README.md Quickstart step 1 (after "Re-running is safe."): one sentence that the folder need not be a git repository -- the first start initialises one on main with a seed commit (.gitignore, orca.yaml, the tracker) because Orca cannot create a workspace without a base branch, and the folder's own files stay untracked until added. README.md provision list (~line 413, "the first-run seeds, the git identity, the tracker, the `orca repo add`"): insert "the repository itself (initialised on `main` with a seed commit when the folder is not one, or has no commits yet)". CLAUDE.md Architecture Overview list ("the config sync, the seeds, `bd init`, `orca repo add`"): insert "the git init" with a parenthetical of the same content, one clause.

BOUNDARIES. Do not touch provision-run.sh, 50-seed-project, 60-orca-repo-add, seed-project.sh, launcher.sh, bootstrap.sh, entrypoint.sh, run-tests.sh or any existing test. Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines, one file per response; report under 60 lines: files changed, the TAP plan lines, any 'not ok', and any deviation from this spec. Commit on your branch with `git add -- <paths>` and `git commit -m ... -- <paths>` (never a bare git commit, never amend/reset/stash); subject: "provision: 55-git-init -- a folder that is not a repository, or has no commits, gets main and a seed commit before orca repo add (UNVERIFIED on a Mac)".

description:

Remove the per-folder profile entirely: no orca_profile_* helpers, no ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH on any CLI call, launch is plain `open` with the app flag and the found app (no -n, no --args), teardown runs environment rm only. title: container: provision step sweeps stale worktrees at every start (clean ones removed through Orca, dirty or busy ones kept and reported)
description:
WHY
Nothing in the repo ever removes a worktree (orca-run.sh, delegate.sh and by-hand executors all create them; no script calls `orca worktree rm` or `git worktree remove`). Orca rediscovers every git worktree from .git/worktrees at load and lists each as a workspace under the project, so the user's sidebar filled with "claude-orca (Detached HEAD)", "wt/dbu", "wt/tests-b". The user wants that noise cleared by the script.

WHAT
A new step scripts/container/provision.d/65-worktree-sweep following the provision.d conventions (sources provision-lib.sh; idempotent; never fatal; writes the row `provision status` reads). For every worktree of PROJECT_DIR from `git worktree list --porcelain` other than the main one:
- directory missing -> `git worktree prune` covers it; log "pruned <path>".
- some process has its cwd inside it (scan /proc/[0-9]*/cwd; readlink) -> keep; log "busy <path>".
- `git -C <path> status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` empty -> remove: when `orca-ide status --json` reports .result.runtime.reachable == true use `orca-ide worktree rm --worktree path:<path> --json` (Orca also drops the branch when it can prove it merged, keeps it otherwise); when Orca is unreachable use `git worktree remove <path>`; then `git worktree prune`; log "removed <path>".
- otherwise (uncommitted or untracked files) -> keep; log "kept <path>: uncommitted changes".
Status: ok when nothing was kept for uncommitted changes (busy is ok); FAIL naming each kept-dirty path otherwise, so the SessionStart hook surfaces it at the first prompt and Claude deals with it. The CLI is resolved the way the other steps resolve orca-ide (read 60-orca-repo-add).

Check how existing provision tests build a fixture (tests/container-provision*.bats, tests/container-entrypoint.bats) and mirror it: a throwaway git repo as PROJECT_DIR with real `git worktree add`, a stub orca-ide on PATH whose `status --json` reachability and `worktree rm` behaviour are driven by env vars and which records its argv.

BOUNDARIES: no change to entrypoint.sh, other steps, or the Mac side. Copy the PASS-IF case names verbatim into @test lines, one per named case. title: desktop conduit: launch Orca.app on a launcher-owned profile that holds only this folder's environment; zero local projects, fail-closed
description:
WHY
The user's rule: nothing the launcher opens may run outside the container, no exception. Orca.app 1.4.197 can open LOCAL workspaces (allowLocalRuntime = !isWebClient, no knob), and today the launcher launches the user's own Orca profile, which already held this folder as a local project (badge "Local Mac"). Detection at hand-off (c4c5a4b) is not enough.

WHAT (scripts/launcher.sh, Mac side, bash 3.2)
1. A launcher-owned profile per folder: <project>/.claude-dev/state/orca-profile (mkdir -p, chmod 700). Helper orca_profile_dir "$dir". It is the app's user-data dir for THIS folder and holds only this folder's environment. The user's own Orca profile is never touched again.
2. Every orca CLI call the launcher makes (orca_hand_off: status/environment rm/add; orca_env_forget; cmd_verify's local-repos row; any other cli call) runs with ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<profile> in its environment (verified fact: the CLI resolves the instance per that env var; `status --json` under an empty profile reports reachable:false).
3. Launch: `open -n`, the app flag naming Orca.app as today, then `--args --user-data-dir=<profile>` (a new instance on our profile; the user's Orca keeps running on theirs). Skip the launch when `status --json` under the profile already reports reachable (an earlier ./claude-dev left the conduit running). CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=0 still skips it.
4. Before every launch: if <profile>/orca-data.json exists and its .repos is non-empty, rewrite it with .repos = [] through jq (write to a temp file in the profile, then mv). The conduit starts every session with zero local projects.
5. Fail closed at hand-off and in verify: `repo list --json` under the profile listing ANY repo (not just this folder) is the leak. print_desktop_block_v3's orca_local_leak_note: keep the WARNING, worded for the conduit ("this folder's Orca profile holds a LOCAL project ... it will be removed at the next ./claude-dev; ./claude-dev verify reports it"), and cmd_verify's "local repos" row FAILs on any repo, ok on none, and also FAILs when ui=desktop and the profile dir is missing. Reuse orca_lists_local_repo or replace it with an any-repo check -- keep the function names the tests already use where possible.
6. Teardown: orca_env_forget runs environment rm under the profile, then rm -rf the profile dir.
7. README.md desktop section: three sentences -- the app is launched on a private per-folder profile holding only the container's environment; it starts with no local projects and the launcher empties any before each launch; the app's own "+ Add project" cannot be disabled in 1.4.197, so a local project added mid-session lives until the next ./claude-dev and verify reports it meanwhile.

Subagent calls stay skipped entirely. lane express keeps its current exemption.
2. scripts/output-cap.sh, a PreToolUse hook on Bash: main loop only; skipped when tool_input.run_in_background is true, when CLAUDE_ORCA_OUTPUT_CAP is 0, or when the command already ends in a pipe to head/tail/wc. Otherwise it rewrites tool_input.command through hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput (the tier-gate.sh precedent) into a wrapper that runs the original command with stdout+stderr into a file under ${CLAUDE_ORCA_OUTPUT_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude-orca-output/<session_id>}, prints the first CLAUDE_ORCA_OUTPUT_CAP bytes (default 6000), appends one line '[output capped at N bytes of M; full output: <path>]' only when it was cut, and exits with the original command's exit code. The wrapper must survive commands containing single quotes, heredocs and && chains: write the original command to a file and run it with 'bash <file>' rather than interpolating it.
3. config/claude-settings.json: register output-cap on PreToolUse matcher Bash AFTER the existing guards; add "subagentPromptCacheTtl": "1h" at top level.

title: A: dispatch reliability -- heartbeat, stall rule with nudge and fallback, launch diagnostics, new-child naming, stagger
description:
Slice A -- dispatch reliability (Win 1). Files: scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/orca-wait.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, NEW tests/orca-wait.bats, NEW tests/orca-dispatch-launch.bats (both driven by a stub orca-ide/orca on PATH that replays canned JSON from fixture files and logs every argv to a file; the existing tests/orca-dispatch.bats uses the real xvfb CLI and is not part of this contract).
Behaviour:
1. The dispatch record (.claude-dev/run/orchestration/dispatch/<id>.json) gains started_at (epoch seconds) and worktree_path (the directory behind a path: selector, else empty).
2. orca-wait gains --stall-after <sec> (default 600) and --poll <sec> (default 60): it loops on 'orchestration check --wait' in poll-sized waits until the overall --timeout-ms, and between waits inspects every dispatch record in state ready/running. Activity for a record = the newest of: started_at, the time of the last heartbeat/question/escalation message seen from that dispatch (persist last_activity in the record when a message arrives), the HEAD commit time of worktree_path, and the newest mtime among files 'git -C worktree_path status --porcelain' lists. If now - activity > stall-after: print one receipt {"type":"stalled","bead","dispatch_id","terminal","idle_s","nudge":"orca terminal send --terminal <h> --text ... --enter"} and, unless --no-nudge, send exactly one nudge through 'orca terminal send' telling the worker to continue and to heartbeat, recording nudged_at in the record. If a record already has nudged_at and stalls again, print {"type":"stalled","nudged":true,"fallback":"<the Agent-tool spec, as orch_fallback prints it>","worktree_path":...} and return 0 so the orchestrator can re-run the slice in-process on the same worktree.
3. WORKER RULES (orch_spec in lib/orca-orch.sh) gain one rule: after every commit and at least every 5 minutes of work, send 'orca-ide orchestration send --type heartbeat --subject alive --task-id <t> --dispatch-id <d> --json'; and orca-wait treats a heartbeat as activity without printing a receipt for it beyond one stderr note.
4. orca-dispatch: --worktree new-child passes --name wt/<bead-id> to worker-start (and the worktree_path recorded is whatever worker-start's JSON reports). When worker-start reports state failed, read the terminal ('orca terminal read --terminal <h> --json'), store its last 8 non-empty lines as launch_tail in the record, print the receipt with reason=<last line> on STDERR, print the Agent-tool fallback spec (orch_fallback) on STDOUT and exit 3 -- the same contract the unreachable-runtime path already has -- so the orchestrator falls back at once instead of guessing.
5. Stagger: before worker-start, if the newest dispatch record was written less than CLAUDE_ORCA_DISPATCH_STAGGER_MS (default 5000) ago, sleep the remainder, so a fan-out wave shares the first worker's cached prefix and does not burst the per-minute rate limit.
bash 3.2 clean (scripts/ is scanned). Keep tests/orca-dispatch.bats green (run it once; it needs the xvfb CLI, if that is unavailable here say so and do not edit it).

title: S2: app discovery and the ui key -- bootstrap preflight finds Orca.app, register writes ui desktop|web, doctor rows

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# claude-orca-xyr CHECK: a SECOND folder whose template clone comes from
# origin (GitHub, the way bootstrap and --update deliver it) runs ITS OWN
# config-sync and ends up with no /card command and no card hook entry.
set -uo pipefail
ORIGIN="https://github.com/joe-rayment/claude_orca.git"
WORK="${1:?usage: xyr-check.sh <scratch-dir>}"
FOLDER="$WORK/second-folder"
rm -rf "$FOLDER"
mkdir -p "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/home" "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/run"
echo '{}' > "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/claude-orca.json"

echo "== 1. template clone from origin/main"
git clone -q --branch main "$ORIGIN" "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/template" || { echo "FAIL clone"; exit 1; }
sha=$(git -C "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/template" rev-parse HEAD)
echo "template HEAD = $sha"

echo "== 2. the FOLDER's own config-sync, ambient identity stripped"
env -u PROJECT_DIR -u CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT -u CLAUDE_ORCA_HOST_DIR -u CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR \
    HOME="$FOLDER/.claude-dev/home" \
    "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/template/scripts/config-sync.sh" \
        --project "$FOLDER" --host "$FOLDER/.claude-dev" \
    || { echo "FAIL config-sync exit $?"; exit 1; }

CFG="$FOLDER/.claude-dev/home/.claude"
echo "== 3. assertions on $CFG"
fail=0
if [ -e "$CFG/commands/card.md" ]; then echo "FAIL commands/card.md present"; fail=1
else echo "ok   no commands/card.md"; fi
ls "$CFG/commands" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/     commands: /'

n=$(jq '[.hooks[][].hooks[].command | select(test("bin/card"))] | length' "$CFG/settings.json") \
    || { echo "FAIL settings.json unreadable"; exit 1; }
if [ "$n" = "0" ]; then echo "ok   0 hook entries match bin/card"
else echo "FAIL $n hook entries match bin/card"; fail=1; fi

if grep -qiE '(^|[^a-z])card([^a-z]|$)' "$CFG/settings.json"; then
    echo "FAIL the word 'card' appears in the synced settings.json"; fail=1
else echo "ok   no word 'card' in the synced settings.json"; fi

total=$(jq '[.hooks[][].hooks[]] | length' "$CFG/settings.json")
echo "     $total hook entries synced in total (non-vacuous: the sync ran)"
[ "$total" -gt 0 ] || { echo "FAIL no hook entries at all -- sync did not run"; fail=1; }

if [ "$fail" = 0 ]; then echo "PASS xyr: second folder at origin/main $sha carries no /card"
else echo "FAIL xyr"; fi
exit "$fail"

title: OpenRouter guard: the real key is visible via ps/proc to any same-uid process while the guard runs (argv/environ), not just to the guard itself
description: Found by the qa2.21 verifier, does not affect that bead's PASS. entrypoint.sh starts the guard as 'env OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<real key> python3 <guard script> ...', so the key sits in that process's argv and /proc/<pid>/environ, readable by any process running as the same agent uid (e.g. a worker terminal doing ps -ef or reading /proc). The guard's whole purpose is to keep the key out of agent terminals' reach, so this is a real if narrow gap: an agent that specifically goes looking (ps -ef | grep OPENROUTER, or reads /proc/<guard-pid>/environ) can still recover the real key, though normal agent env/config never shows it. Fix: pass the key to the guard via a pipe/fd or a mode-600 file read once at startup instead of argv/env, and have the guard scrub it from its own os.environ immediately after reading (argv still needs care: use env -u or read from stdin instead of an argv assignment).
notes: RED-AT e62e105 · GREEN-AT 9f99786 (wt/dbu). Verifier PASS: frozen diff empty; red not ok 19,20 (entrypoint) and 12 (provision); green 1..20 and 1..17 zero not ok, names verbatim; syntax/py_compile clean. Real guard started with a dummy key file: listening, /proc/<pid>/environ key matches 0, cmdline matches 0, no OPENROUTER_API_KEY line at all, key file unlinked, guard.log matches 0; whitespace-only key file -> exit 2, unlinked, logged. Mechanism: mode-600 agent-owned key file read once and unlinked, guard started with env -u, os.environ popped, provision-run's handoff also a key file unlinked on read, step 70 unsets before a restart (a real leak the restart case caught: /proc/<pid>/environ is fixed at exec, so env -u is load-bearing). Verifier note: read_api_key() keeps an OPENROUTER_API_KEY env fallback for by-hand runs, documented, unused by the image. Follow-up bead for the Mac run: claude-orca-1ca.

title: S9 Opt-in Orca orchestration mode (orca CLI socket inside the sandbox, skills, hardening checklist)
description:
Why: Orca's orchestration layer (runs, tasks, `orca orchestration worker-start --agent codex --worktree current`, messages, gates) is the most native way for Claude to direct other models and have Orca show every worker. But the orca CLI socket is a remote control for an unsandboxed app: `orca terminal create --command …` runs anything outside the sandbox unless the shell is in one of this project's worktrees, `orca goto/exec` drives an unsandboxed browser (network escape), automations and artifacts run outside too. So this is opt-in, off by default, and the residual surface is stated every time it is on.

What: <project>/.claude-dev/sandbox.json `{"orca": {"cli": true}}` → the wrapper adds allowUnixSockets [<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca] and allowRead of that dir, passes ORCA_CLI_COMMAND through, installs the orca-cli + orchestration skills into the config dir (from the Orca repo's skills/, pinned copy under template/), and adds a rulebook addendum: Claude is the coordinator; a tier's executor slice may become `orca orchestration worker-start --task <id> --worktree current --agent <codex|claude|gemini>` (same worktree → sandboxed by S2); workers report worker_done; beads remain the source of truth. `claude-dev --doctor` prints the escape-surface warning and the Orca settings to harden (Floating Workspace off, public artifact links off, no per-repo setup hooks) whenever the mode is on. The self-test's orca-socket probe expects reachable in this mode.

Boundaries: no attempt to sandbox Orca itself.
